name: Tilly
description:
I would like a home filled with love and kindness!

I would prefer to be an only dog but could live with another laid back dog.

I'd like a secure garden to potter around in.

I am learning all about walking on a lead and harness, but need more practice.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am spayed and have several teeth extracted and was already missing a few!

Tilly is a very sweet but extremely nervous girly who has come into our care from a breeder. When she arrived she first arrived she was very nervous and completely overwhelmed to find herself here, but since then she has really come out of her shell and blossomed into the sweetest, affectionate girl and confidence has grown so much.

Tilly is now confident enough that we would consider homing her as an only dog, in the right circumstances with adopters who have had ex-breeding dogs before and who are around most of the time. We feel like she may even prefer to be homed as an only dog as the more confident she has become, the less she enjoys sharing attention with other dogs and would prefer to have all the love for herself. Despite this, she does socialise very well with other dogs and if she was to be homed as an only dog she would still enjoy socialising with other dogs often. We would consider homing her with another laid back dog who wouldn't mind Tilly craving all the effection. We would also consider homing her with gentle, dog savvy teenagers.

As Tilly has never lived in a home before, he adopters will need to be kind and understanding as she learns all about home life and new skills like house training. She has started learning all about walking on a lead and harness but has only managed to take a few steps so far and much prefers to be carried at the moment!

Tilly is a wonderful little girl and in the right home we think she is going to truly thrive and become your absolute best friend, so please don't leave her waiting!

She has had a dental with us where she had 12 teeth extracted and our vet noted that she was already missing 15, so she will benefit from a soft food diet moving forwards.

Tilly has been given the Gift of Life by Laura Midwinter-Brown

Tilly is a very sweet but extremely nervous girly who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start.

Tilly will need plenty of time to settle into her new home, as she is not comfortable being handled at the moment. Her adopters will need to be patient and take things slowly, allowing her to go at her own pace so that she does not feel overwhelmed. She will need gentle encouragement and the chance to build trust in her own time.

Tilly will need another kind and confident dog in her new home. This dog will be a much-needed support system for her, helping to guide her and give her the reassurance she needs as she settles in and finds her paws.

As Tilly has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training and the other basics of home life. Her new family will need to understand that these things may take time and be willing to work with her at a pace she can manage.

Tilly's adopters will need to have ex-breeding experience to better understand her needs. She can live with older dog-savvy children that are sensible and understand she needs a quiet environment she can settle into. A calm environment, patient adopters and a reassuring canine companion will be important in helping her feel safe.

Tilly is a very worried little girl who will need understanding and patience to help her adjust to a new way of life. We hope that with the right support and plenty of time, she will gradually learn to trust and begin to enjoy the love and comfort of a home of her own.

name: Benji
description:
I could live with older, dog-savvy teens who respect my space.

I can be an only dog or live with other dogs. I have never met cats.

I'd like a secure garden to have fun playtimes in.

I walk on a lead and would enjoy a nice walk once a day.

I have lived in a home so I know the basics.

03-11-26 Benji is a beautiful, playful boy who originally came into our care as an unclaimed dog in 2024. He was adopted but has sadly returned to us because of illness in the family, meaning his owners were no longer able to care for him.

Benji is feeling a little out of sorts being back in kennels but is coping well. He is a super-loving boy who absolutely adores attention, cuddles and bum scratches. He has been spending lots of time in the office with us while his exercise is restricted and is always happy to soak up some fuss. He has lots of character and a wonderfully silly personality, and we know he would love nothing more than to be back in a home where he can relax on the sofa and enjoy life with his favourite people!

Benji can be a little reactive towards other dogs when out on walks, but having spent time in a home, he has made some lovely improvements. He is currently kennelled with a friend and we feel he could potentially live with another suitable dog or as an only dog. His adopters will need to be understanding of his needs and willing to continue supporting him with his training around other dogs. When Benji was initially with us, he could snap at feet when leaving his kennel, but this behaviour has improved massively since his time in a home. He is generally much better around doorways, although he can still become uncomfortable if someone lingers in a doorway or enters without greeting him, so his adopters will need to be mindful of this.

Having lived in a home before, Benji is familiar with the sights and sounds of everyday life and will hopefully settle back into a home routine with a little time. He needs a calm home with adopters who understand his breed and can give him the consistency and reassurance he needs. He can live with teenagers aged 16 and over who understand his needs and will respect his space.

Benji was castrated and had nasal wedge surgery in 2024. He can still experience episodes of being sick, particularly following exercise, excitement or periods of stress. He is currently being trialled on a course of medication to see whether this helps manage his symptoms, but he may require further investigation and potentially additional surgery to address his breathing, such as BOAS surgery, in the future. His exercise and activity levels are currently being managed, so he will need adopters who are happy to accommodate his reduced exercise needs and understand that he may require further veterinary treatment and monitoring as needed.

Benji really is a lovely little man who is full of character and has so much love to give. He is a typical silly Frenchie who is desperate to get back to being the couch potato he deserves to be! With a calm home, understanding adopters and plenty of cuddles, we know he will be so happy to have a sofa to call his own again.

name: Jules
description:
I can live with older children, aged 16+, who understand I need time to settle in.

I will need a kind resident dog in my new home. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I haven't tried walks just yet and will find this a bit overwhelming at the moment.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have had 32 teeth removed and will need a soft food diet.

21-09-26 Jules has come to us from a breeder to start her new adventure. She is a very nervous girl who is feeling overwhelmed by all the changes in her world. She is unsure of people and worried about being handled, so will initially run away and hide. She is a sweet girl underneath her worries, and we hope that with kindness, reassurance and time, she will slowly learn that people can be trusted.

Jules will be looking for a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with scared ex-breeding dogs and understand that she will need to settle in completely at her own pace. We would consider a home with gentle, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16+ who can give her the space and patience she needs.

Jules will need a kind and confident resident dog in her new home to take her under their wing and help her feel safe as she adjusts to home life. Having a canine friend to learn from will be important for Jules as she begins to build her confidence and discover that the world isn't such a scary place.

Jules has never lived in a home before, so she will need kind and patient adopters as she learns all about home life and new skills like house training. She will also need to learn about walking on a lead and harness, starting with gentle practice around the garden and gradually building her confidence.

Jules is a sweet girl who has so much potential, and in the right home, we hope she will truly thrive. With patience, understanding and the support of a confident canine companion, she can begin to feel safe and discover just how wonderful life can be.

Our vets have noted that Jules has ectropion affecting her lower eyelids, which has been assessed but required no treatment. She has had 32 teeth removed at the time of her spay and will need a soft food diet moving forwards.

description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog my size or larger to help me settle in & I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have an undershot jaw & I have had 4 of my teeth removed during spay!

27-08-26 Sunny is a sweet girl who has come to us from a breeder and is trying her hardest to be brave. She was very briefly adopted, but after a few days in her new home it was clear that her and the resident dog weren't a good match and so she has returned to our care.

Sunny loves other dogs and still looks to her kennel friends for comfort and reassurance, so she will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home who she can look to and lean on as she continues to grow in confidence. We think she will settle quickly in the right home, and with patience and encouragement, we’re sure her lovely personality will really begin to shine.

She has started to learn all about walking on a lead and harness and though this is still new to her, she is doing well. Sunny is an amazing lady who has so much to look forward to and will make a wonderful addition to a loving and accepting home.

Sunny has arrived with an undershot jaw that does not seem to bother her, but will need to be monitored in her new home. She has had 4 teeth removed at the time of her spay.

If you have a house full of toys, love and cosy beds, please consider welcoming this cheeky little darling.

name: Louise
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home with experienced adopters.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I am not ready to learn about lead walking yet. A garden is fine for now.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

Louise has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for a very special forever home. She is an extremely worried little girl who has had very little positive human socialisation and can still find people and handling very frightening. However, she has made lovely progress since arriving and is showing us more of her cheeky personality every day.

Over the past month, Louise has grown in confidence. While she is still very worried about being touched and picked up, she is no longer as shut down as she was when she first arrived. She is now more than happy to come over for treats and will sit close by while waiting for more. She likes to use her voice to let everyone know how she is feeling, is very partial to chasing flies, and has quite a big personality packed into such a tiny dog. It is wonderful to see her becoming more comfortable in her surroundings.

Louise will need a calm and quiet adult-only home with no visiting children, and adopters who have experience helping fearful ex-breeding dogs learn to trust. She relies heavily on the comfort and reassurance of other dogs and will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help guide her as she settles into family life.

Louise can be vocal around food and may give a warning growl, but she does not actually do anything and this appears to simply be her way of communicating that she would like some space. She can happily be fed alongside her canine friends as long as each dog has their own bowl and they stick to their own food. She is also absolutely fine taking treats, so this is something her adopters should continue to manage calmly and sensibly.

Louise is slowly becoming more comfortable with being handled, and gentle work has begun to help her get used to being picked up. This is still very worrying for her and she can become wriggly and panic when lifted, but she has never tried to bite during these sessions. With time and patience, we hope she will continue to learn that she is safe and that nobody is going to hurt her.

Having never lived in a home before, Louise has lots to learn. Her adopters will need to be patient and understanding as she adjusts to home life and learns the basics, including house training. She is not yet ready for harness training, so her future family will need to carefully plan how and when to introduce this once she feels more secure. Everything must happen at Louise's pace so that she can continue building confidence without becoming overwhelmed.

Louise is a sensitive little soul who will need a dedicated home willing to invest time, patience and understanding into helping her flourish. Every small step she takes is a huge achievement, and she continues to surprise us with just how much she is growing in confidence. With experienced adopters, kind canine companions and lots of love, we truly believe Louise will continue to blossom into the wonderful little dog we know she can become.

Louise has been given the Gift of Life by Ann Winter

Louise has been with us for about 3 months now and even though she has progressed since she first arrived, things are happening very slowly and steadily. I would have liked for her to have gained more confidence by this point, but some dogs struggle with being in such a busy kennel environment to let their guard down … and Louise is one of them! That’s okay though. Making sure she’s happy and content within herself is the most important thing, and I’d say she is!

I haven’t really pushed Louise too far out of her comfort zone up until now, just because I didn’t want to send her backwards with her progress, but there does come a point where you have to, to prove to them that it’s okay. So today I took Louise into my grooming room for a very gentle and calm brushing session. She didn’t want to stand on the grooming table and kept clambering back onto me - which is the first time she’s ever done that - so I opted to keep her on my lap while I brushed her. She was settled for the most part, but she did have a little panic when we got to her ears as she had a couple of tangles which must have hurt her. I managed to cut them out with a scissors and then she was okay with me brushing around that area. I kept the session very short and sweet as I didn’t want to push too far, and I think it was the right decision. When I took her back to the kennel she didn’t sprint away from me or anything like that, so I’d say our relationship is still there!

Louise is such a special little character, and I really hope someone will see her in the same way I do soon. She deserves a life outside of kennels, one where she can finally start to thrive.

Louise has been on my section with me for about a month now, and I’ve definitely seen some positive changes in her. She’s still terrified of being touched and picked up, but her overall confidence is improving daily. She’s now more than happy to come and take treats from me and sit close to me while she’s waiting for more. She’s also nowhere near as shut down as she was when she first arrived and is now turning into quite a cheeky monkey. She does like to use her voice to express her feelings, and she’s also very partial to chasing flies! She’s actually got quite a big personality for such a little girl, and it’s a pleasure to see it emerging as the days go by.I’ve been working slowly on getting Louise used to being picked up, and while she’s definitely still very worried about it, she has calmed down slightly. She’s never tried to bite me, but she does sometimes have little panics and becomes very wriggly when she’s in my arms. I do think this is something that will improve over time. She just needs some more practice and to realise that we’re not hurting her. She obviously hasn’t been handled a lot in her life, so now it’s up to us to prove to her that it’s okay.I love working with Louise, and I can really see the potential in her. She just needs someone to give her a chance and work with her through all her worries and fears. She’s not ready for harness training or conquering the outside world yet, so that’s something her future adopters will need to take into consideration and make a plan for. I do believe she’ll progress faster in a kind home with adopters who have lots of time and patience to give her, so I really hope she won’t have to wait here for much longer.

Louise has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for a very special forever home. She is an extremely worried little girl who has had very little positive human socialisation and currently finds people and handling very frightening. At the moment, Louise feels safest keeping her distance and, if pushed beyond her comfort zone, may make the wrong decision and nip purely out of fear. She is a very scared girl who needs understanding, patience and time.Louise will need a calm and quiet adult-only home with no visiting children, and adopters who have experience of helping fearful ex-breeding dogs learn to trust. She relies heavily on the comfort and reassurance of other dogs and will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home who can take her under their wing.Although Louise takes great comfort from other dogs, she can show signs of resource guarding around food. For this reason, she will need to be fed separately from other dogs, and care will need to be taken when giving treats or other high-value food items. Her adopters will need experience of managing this behaviour and the confidence to do so appropriately.Having never lived in a home before, Louise has lots to learn. Her adopters will need to be patient and understanding as she adjusts to home life and learns new skills such as house training. She is not yet ready to begin learning about lead walking or wearing a harness, as handling is still very worrying for her. These things will need to be introduced gradually and at her pace once she feels more comfortable and secure.Louise is a sensitive soul who will need a dedicated home willing to invest time, patience and understanding into helping her build confidence. We will continue to work with her every day, helping her take small steps forward at a pace she is comfortable with. In the right home, with the support of canine friends and experienced adopters, we hope Louise will slowly learn that people can be kind and that life has so much to offer.

name: Crispin
description:
I would like a calm and quiet home where I can settle in.

I would prefer to be the only dog in the home. I don't mind cats!

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I walk well on a lead and love being out and about!

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

Crispin originally came to us from a breeder last October. He was adopted for a few months but returned to our care after his adopters sadly realised they were not the right match for him. Although they gave him every opportunity to settle, Crispin remained very worried whenever the male in the household was home and struggled to relax in his company.

Since returning to us, Crispin has moved into foster and has settled beautifully. He is an incredibly loving, cuddly little boy who simply wants to be close to his people. While he can initially be worried by some men, his foster carer has found that once visitors give him some attention, he quickly relaxes and happily cuddles up with them. He does the same with female visitors. He has adult grandsons in his foster home and, after an initial bark, is very happy to settle down with them.

Crispin does get on with other dogs, but he can be quite keen to push his way in for attention and may grumble if another dog gets in the way. He is not aggressive and, having no teeth, cannot bite, but he would be best suited to being homed as an only dog. His foster carer feels he would particularly enjoy being the centre of his person's world, as he simply loves being with his human, male or female.

Crispin absolutely loves his walks and this is his favourite pastime. He gets wonderfully excited when it is time to go out and walks beautifully on both a lead and harness. He is sociable with other dogs he meets, enjoys exploring new places and travels well in the car. He particularly loves visiting the coffee shop and is happiest when he can be out and about with his people.

As Crispin has now experienced life in a home, he has settled well into a routine and sleeps soundly through the night. He has had the occasional wee indoors first thing in the morning, although this has been improving, so his adopters should continue his house training with patience and consistency.

Crispin forms incredibly strong bonds with his favourite people and loves to be close by and involved in everything they are doing. He showed signs of separation anxiety in his previous home when left for more than a couple of hours, so his ideal home would be one where someone is around for most of the day and any time alone can be built up gradually.

Crispin has a cataract in his right eye and is developing one in his left. Despite this, he gets around brilliantly and you would hardly know he has eyesight problems. He has also had all of his teeth removed and will need to remain on a soft diet for life. He has Grade 2 patella luxation in both hind legs, which may continue to improve with gentle exercise as

Crispin has a travel document, which says he is 7 years old, but we do feel he could potentially be a little older than this.

Crispin has been given the Gift of Life by Katrina Pirner

Crispin has continued to make lovely progress in foster, and his foster mum has learned a lot more about what makes him tick. When he first arrived after being returned due to struggling to settle with the male member of his previous household, it was felt that he would be happiest as an only dog. He was very people-focused and wanted all the attention to himself, often pushing the resident dogs out of the way if they came looking for fuss. However, as he has settled and grown more comfortable, he has shown that he is much happier sharing his people than first thought!

Crispin now gets along well with the resident dogs and absolutely adores them. He has also enjoyed meeting other dogs when out in secure fields. He can initially bark at visitors, but has learned that they are friendly and will happily accept cuddles and attention from them. When meeting new people and their dogs, he can still look for a little reassurance from his human, but once he knows everything is okay, he is happy to go off and enjoy himself with the other dogs.

Crispin has excellent recall in secure areas and regularly checks in with his foster mum for a little fuss and reassurance before heading off to explore again.

We now feel Crispin could be happy either as an only dog or living with another calm, friendly dog who is comfortable sharing their humans. His adopters will need to understand his little quirks and be prepared to offer reassurance when he is unsure of a situation. With the right understanding and consistency, Crispin has shown that he can happily share his home and his people.

Crispin is looking for his own special human where he can be the ONLY dog and have all the love and affection for himself. Although he is in foster with other dogs, we think he would now prefer to be the only dog in the home.

Crispin has recently spent a few days with another fosterer as I was on holiday and attached himself to the lady of the house and wasn't interested in the other 5 dogs or man of the house just the lady.

He walks perfectly on the lead and loves to go out as many times as you're willing to take him, equally though he loves to potter in the garden alongside his fosterer whilst she's raking up leaves. He loves to settle inside either on your lap or close by on the sofa.

Crispin enjoys all foods though some treats have to be in small pieces as he has no teeth but he eats either wet food or kibble with warm water to mash it down. His cataract doesn't affect him at all. Although Crispin is 7 he has the energy and zest for life of a much younger dog. He can literally walk for hours.

Crispin would love a one person, male or female, calm household where he can soak up all the attention from his special human. Although he gets on with all dogs outside of the home, he prefers to be cuddled up with his human wherever it may be.. sofa, bed he s not fussed as long as he knows they are close by him.

Crispin walks perfectly on a harness and lead and is good off lead too. He will walk ahead of you but keep coming back to 'check in' with you.

Crispin continues to thrive in his foster home and is loving this home life. He loves his food, loves his walks, loves his cuddles and just loves everything to be honest.

Although Crispin lives alongside his foster sisters, I do feel he would love a home with no other dogs and just a single active  adult home, male or female, where he can have all the attention and love. Cats are fine, as he dosen't take any notice of them.

Although his initial write states that he may be older than 7 I feel he is aged about right apart from his lack of teeth as he is full of energy and  fun.

Crispin is smashing this home life. He is an absolute gentleman and will make a perfect best friend for an active person who is at home most of the time.

This week he has visited various secure fields, visited coffee shops and even popped into a pub for a cool drink while out on a street walk. He loves to be out and about with his human and then return home for snuggles on the sofa.

Although Crispin has a cataract in his right eye this does not seem to affect him at all. His luxating patellas also don't seem to bother him and his movement is 100%.

Crispin recently moved foster homes through no fault of his own. He is a gorgeous, well mannered, cuddly boy who loves his walks, his humans and his food.

He gets along with the cats and dogs in my home, though initially Crispin demanded all the attention and would push the other dogs out of the way to get his cuddles first but with careful handling this has improved over the week.

He loves to cuddle up on my bed with my own dogs and sleeps all night there. He lives for his walks and gets very excited when his lead/harness appear. He can walk on his own or with another dog for company.

He happily shares his food bowl with his foster friend Lemon Pie. Even the cats dig in with him sometimes. He is getting used to being left when I go shopping and I am extending these trips so he gets used to being without humans for a while. Crispin does bark initially when visitors come into my home but this soon subsides when he realises they will do him no harm. Keep up the good work Crispin, you've got this my boy

Crispin has been back in foster care for a week and has settled in beautifully. He is an incredibly loving, cuddly little boy who simply wants to be loved. Sadly, he was returned because he became anxious and barked whenever the man in the household moved around.

He walks beautifully on a lead and harness, sleeps soundly through the night alongside the other foster dog, and travels well. Although he is perfectly happy living with other dogs, he could also be an only dog so he can enjoy all the cuddles and affection he deserves. He has had a few little accidents indoors first thing in the morning, but over the last few days he has settled into a much better routine.

Crispin has no teeth, so he will need to remain on a soft diet for the rest of his life. He also has a cataract in one eye and the beginnings of a cataract in the other, but you would hardly know he has any sight issues as he gets around so well.

He really is a very special little boy who simply needs a loving home where he can feel safe, secure, and cherished.

Crispin originally came to us from a breeder last October. He was adopted for a few months but has come back into our care after his adopters sadly realised they were not the right match for him. Although they gave him every opportunity to settle, Crispin remained very worried whenever the male in the household was home and simply couldn't relax in his company.Crispin is a dear little boy who can still be worried and unsure at times. It is clear that he had very little socialisation in the past, and although he has made lovely progress since living in a home, he still needs patient adopters who understand that building trust takes time. He can be touch-sensitive when he is feeling anxious, so gentle handling and allowing him to approach in his own time will help him continue to gain confidence.Crispin will be best suited to adopters who understand the needs of scared ex-breeding dogs and who will give him all the time he needs to settle at his own pace. He would be happy to share his home with another kind and confident resident dog in his new home. However, in the right home, with owners who are around enough to reassure him and who have experience with ex-breeding dogs, he could also be the only dog in the home.One thing Crispin has discovered is just how much he loves going for walks! He gets wonderfully excited when it's time to head out, twirling around and eagerly waiting by the front door. Once out, he walks beautifully on a lead, is very sociable with other dogs he meets, enjoys exploring new places, and travels well in the car. Walking has become one of his favourite activities and is a lovely way to watch his confidence shine through.As Crispin has now experienced life in a home, he has become familiar with many of the sights and sounds of everyday living. However, he hasn't quite mastered house training yet, so his adopters will need to continue helping him learn with patience, consistency, and plenty of encouragement.Crispin has also shown that he forms incredibly strong bonds with his favourite person. He loves to be close by and wants to be involved in everything they are doing. Because of this, he showed signs of separation anxiety in his previous home when left for more than a couple of hours. His ideal home would therefore be one where someone is around for most of the day, and where any time left alone can be built up very gradually, helping him feel safe and secure.Crispin has a cataract in his right eye and is developing a cataract in his left eye. He has had dental work and unfortunately did need to have all of his teeth removed, so he will need to stay on a soft diet for the rest of his life. He has Grade 2 patella luxation in both hind legs, although this may continue to improve with gentle exercise as he builds muscle.Crispin is a gentle soul who has had a difficult start in life, but he has already shown that, with kindness and patience, he is capable of making wonderful progress. He is looking for a very special person who will understand his worries, celebrate his achievements, and enjoy watching him continue to blossom into the loyal and loving companion we know he can be.Crispin has a travel document, which says he is 7 years old, but we do feel he could be a little older than this.

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. name: Royal
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I would like to live with a female dog. No cats please!

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I can walk on a lead and harness and love to explore quiet areas.

I am learning about house training in my foster home, and am doing so good!

Royal is a very special Chow Chow who has come to us from a breeder in search of his forever home. When he first arrived, he was extremely frightened of the world around him and was very wary of being touched or handled. Thanks to gentle care and patience, Royal has made incredible progress and is continuing to blossom in foster, where he is experiencing home life for the very first time.

Royal has exceeded all expectations with how well he has settled into foster. He has been an absolute superstar, sleeping soundly through the night, travelling well in the car, walking beautifully on lead and has even been completely clean in the house. Every day brings a new milestone, and it has been a joy to watch his confidence grow as he discovers all the comforts and pleasures of family life.

Although Royal is still nervous of people initially, he so desperately wants to trust and tries his hardest to be brave. He has begun asking his foster carers for gentle neck and bum scratches, happily takes treats from their hands, enjoys rummaging through the toy box, has found his little voice and now greets them with his wonderful wagging tail. He is such a sweet, gentle soul who simply needs time to work things out at his own pace.

Royal absolutely relies on the resident female dogs in foster for confidence and reassurance. He watches their every move, learning how to be part of a family, and loves playing alongside them. He will need to share his forever home with at least one kind, confident female dog who enjoys a good play and can continue to show him the way. He cannot live with cats.

As this is Royal's first experience of living in a home, he thrives on routine and will need patient, understanding adopters who will allow him to settle without pressure. He has made remarkable progress already, but he is still very nervous of the unknown and benefits from people who understand that he needs time to process new experiences. A calm, rural or quiet home would suit him best, as he is currently worried by traffic. He is looking for an adult-only home with breed experience and experience with very nervous rescue dogs would be highly beneficial.

Royal has recently had a bath and full groom at the rescue and was an absolute gentleman throughout. As a Chow Chow, his beautiful coat will require regular daily grooming. He is very tolerant of being brushed when it is introduced slowly, little and often, and this has become an important part of his routine.

Royal is an incredibly special boy who has embraced this new chapter in his life with quiet bravery. With patience, kindness and the continued support of confident canine companions, he will become a wonderfully loyal and loving companion. Watching him continue to discover the world and grow in confidence will be an incredibly rewarding journey, and he is sure to make his forever family smile every single day.

Royal is currently being treated for an ear infection.

Wow! This darling boy has just exceeded all expectations with how well he’s settled into his very first home, in his first week. Not a single accident (unheard of for a boy), sleeps soundly over night out of a crate, happy to be left alone with the company of the resident dogs, walks well on a lead, travels well. A literal angel boy.

Royal is the sweetest soul, he doesn’t trust humans easily but he really wants to and tries so hard to be brave.

He relies heavily on our resident girl gang for confidence & reassurance, watching & copying them intently to learn what being a member of a family is all about.

After an initial overwhelming few days for him, every day now brings a new ‘first’ & burst of joy on our part! Asking for a neck / bum scratch, taking a treat from our hand, rummaging in the toy box, playing with the girls, finding his little voice & wagging his amazing tail when we talk to him. He is just loving this next step in life and is so ready to be someone’s special boy.

Royal currently needs an adult only home as has not yet been tested with children. He needs confident kind resident female dogs who like a good play. A rural / quiet location would be preferable as he’s currently quite scared of traffic.

He is still very nervous of the unknown, thrives on routine and needs to be guided and given time to work things out without any pressure so experience with very scared dogs would be helpful.

As a Chow, his beautiful coat will need grooming daily. He is very tolerant of this if done slowly, little & often.

Please get in touch if you feel you might be the right match for this special big guy, he will make you smile every day.

Royal is not a dog I’ve had the chance to work with until recently. I’ve heard a lot about him, as he’s one of our longer stayers. I had heard many great things from other members of staff, including the incredible progress he’s made since joining us!When I did get the chance to work with him, my first impression was “oh my days, you are beautiful!” On first sight, he is one of the most beautiful dogs I’ve ever seen and certainly the most stunning chow I’ve ever seen! How can you look at this handsome boy and not fall in love?!When I actually began working with him, I realised how shy and timid he actually was. Initially, he wouldn’t come to the front of the kennel to see me, he’d hide away in the back. It was evident to me that this boy did not trust me. As I continued to work with him, I was very aware of my actions, to ensure I wasn’t causing any anxiety. I began with treats (who doesn’t love a cheeky bribe?). It slowly worked. Initially, he wanted nothing to do with me. I didn’t want to invade his safe spaces (safe spaces are so important for a more scared or anxious dog. Could you imagine a big scary stranger coming into your home and not leaving? I wouldn’t feel too easy if that occurred to me). So, I’d place the treat and leave the kennel. He’d come out, have a little nosey and take the treat. With time, he began slowly coming out of the back as I entered his kennel. He then began taking treats from my hands and now, whenever I walk onto the section, he comes straight to the gate and waits for me. Honestly, such an incredible feeling making a bond like this with such an incredible boy! There is honestly no feeling like it. They say a dog is a humans best friend but, what no one tells you it works both ways. To build that bond, teach him that I’m not scary, I’m here to help him feel safe, comfortable, happy and to get such a response… it’s honestly the best feeling in the world. Royal needs a home, he needs people to show him this on a day to day basis. We do what we can but, we can’t teach him the safety and comfort of a home, of a family that’s there for him 24/7.Once I got to know this guy a little more, I was taken away. We go out on walks. I feel like this was another bonding experience for us. He loves a walk but, loud noises and interactions with loud people/dogs do freak him out, thus we try to go for quieter walks. He also loves frolicking in the yard. From my experience, he seems to just love being outside!When I worked with him, he didn’t have a friend in his kennel, however, since working with him I have seen him enjoying in the yard with other dogs and is now kennelled with a boxer. He seems very happy. As previously mentioned on his profile, he is to be homed with females around his size or alone. I have not worked with him enough to comment further on his compatibility and amiability with other dogs so, please read the rest of his profile and updates to get a fuller understanding of this incredible boy!At this point, I’ve worked with him enough for him to trust me. He’s happy to see me, he’s fine for me to touch him and fuss him. The Royal I see is a happy dude. He is a scared dog, I’m very aware of that but, the Royal I know now is far different to the Royal I first met. You just have to gain his trust and he’ll let you see him. When you first meet him, he will be shy. He’ll hide and he will not trust you. DO NOT let this deter you. He is one of the sweetest dogs I’ve ever met. From when I first met him to now, I feel like he’s a completely different dog. I was respectful of his boundaries, slow and calm, I did what I could to make him feel comfortable and safe, he then began to trust me and show me his true self (he hides it beneath all that fur). Honestly, I love him. I will take time out of my day to go see him, give him a little treat and some love, just because he is honestly that special. I cannot believe he’s been here over a year. He is one of our most special dogs. I don’t see how anyone can get to know this dog and not love him.Don’t overlook this fluffy dude. Yes, he’s shy and nervous but, the longer you spend with him, care for him and gain his trust, the more you’ll fall in love with him. I can say with confidence; if you put the effort in with Royal, you will fall in love with him.

I absolutely love this boy with my whole heart.

I've been working hard on helping him get used to being brushed because, as a Chow, it's something his future adopters will need to keep up with regularly to keep his coat healthy and prevent mats from developing, especially behind his ears.

Royal is now an absolute angel when it comes to grooming. I brush him every day, and with it being shedding season, no matter how long I brush for, there always seems to be more fur coming out! These days, he simply finds a comfy spot, settles down, and lets me get on with it. If he's had enough, or if I come across a mat that's uncomfortable for him, he communicates so well to let me know he's done for the day.

I also recently decided it was time to give him a bath. I wasn't sure how he'd cope, as it involved picking him up and putting him in the bath, but he was an absolute angel from start to finish. He allowed me to pick him up without any fuss and stood beautifully while I bathed and shampooed him.

I'm so incredibly proud of him. Afterwards, I introduced him to the grooming blower to help remove some of his loose coat. He wasn't a huge fan of it, but he tolerated it for a short while, and I'll continue using it regularly so he can build his confidence with it.

I honestly think all this grooming time has strengthened our bond even more, because lately he seems to be seeking out so much more affection and attention from me. He's such a special boy, and it has been wonderful watching his confidence grow.

Royal has now been with us for over a year, and we’re still waiting for the right person to see just how special he is. He’s had two meet and greets during this time, but sadly neither worked out as he was too nervous meeting new families.

Royal is a sensitive boy who simply needs time, patience, and understanding. He can be unsure at first, but once he begins to trust you, his cheeky, affectionate personality really shines through and it’s such a joy to see.

With a consistent routine, Royal truly thrives. He now enjoys running freely around our large yard without a harness or lead, and when it’s time to go back, he comes straight over. He’s also been out on two longer walks away from the rescue with one of our regular volunteers and has done amazingly well.

All Royal is looking for is someone willing to give him the time and patience he deserves. In return, he’ll become a loyal and loving companion.

I’ve come on leaps and bounds over the past month. I’m still a little shy and can get nervous when I meet new people, but I’m working on it!

I feel most comfortable when I spend quality time with people. It doesn’t take long for me to start feeling at ease (though I still sometimes like my own space). The more time you spend with me, the more comfortable I become—and treats help too! I’ll return your love in equal measure, as long as I’m given the right time, support, and respect.

I love going out for walks, though I can get nervous around loud noises or sudden movements. They might make me jump or feel uneasy, but a bit of love and reassurance always helps!

I feel more comfortable every day. I benefit not only from interaction with my humans, but also from the company of my kennel friends that I live with.

Another month has gone by, and my cheeky boy Royal is still waiting in kennels. I honestly don’t know why this handsome lad isn’t getting much interest. Not only is he completely unique-looking, but he also has the funniest, quirkiest personality. If you want a dog who’ll make you laugh every single day here he is!

Royal is 99% kennel clean and always keeps his bedding tidy… well, until I make his bed perfectly for him. Then he likes to “show me how it’s supposed to be done” by pulling it all across the floor. He walks beautifully on the lead now; he can still get a little spooked from time to time, but he’s made massive progress since the day he arrived.

He loves his toys he just doesn’t love sharing them! He’s also a bit selective with kennel mates, so his ideal home would include a calm, placid large female dog who won’t make too much fuss over him.

Royal truly is an amazing boy, inside and out, and I hope he doesn’t have to wait much longer for the forever home he deserves.

Royal never fails to make us smile with his crazy, funny, and quirky personality. He’s got such a cheeky side to him just waiting for the right people to help it shine.

On the lead, Royal is already walking beautifully, though he can still get a little nervous at times. His new family will need to be patient and willing to help him build confidence. Loud noises or sudden movements can overwhelm him, so he’ll do best with calm, quiet walks to start.

This week Royal had his very first trip down to the big yard! He loved it, though he found his confidence by sticking close to his doggy friend. With more practice, we’re sure he’ll begin to explore on his own.

Royal absolutely adores other dogs. Once he’s settled in, he loves to play, so he’ll need a kind and confident resident dog to show him the ropes, give him reassurance, and of course, enjoy plenty of playtime together.

He’s such a handsome boy with so much love to give we can’t believe he hasn’t found his forever home yet!

This past month has been a huge step forward for our boy Royal! Once a little unsure of the world, Royal is now walking beautifully on lead, it’s such a massive step for him considering how nervous he once was!

Royal currently shares his kennel with both a male and a female dog and he’s proving to be a respectful and easy companion. He enjoys their company, often watching what they do and following their lead. Royal will definitely need another resident dog around his size in his home, so he can continue to have the doggy companionship to help him continue to grow in confidence.

Despite his progress, Royal is still a sensitive soul, and it takes a little time for him to warm up to you. Royals forever family will need to give him time and patience to come out of his shell, so for this reason I believe Royal would be best suited to a home with no children.

Please don’t leave Royal waiting much longer for his forever home, he really deserves a cosy sofa to curl up on!

I’m so proud of Royal, this boy has come on tremendously since arriving at Many Tears. From arriving a terrified dog and very unsure of us humans, he has now slowly but surely begun to trust us and realise we are not so bad, especially when we arrive with cheesy treats.

Royal loves food, toys and being outside in our yards. He has just began harness training, ready to begin lead walking. At the moment he is not so keen on lead walking but he has taken a few tentative steps and with the help of some squeezy cheese and possibly a confident doggie friend to follow I think it won’t be long before he can begin to enjoy exploring the world.

Royals adopters will need to understand he is still very wary and unsure of his environment and he is going to need plenty of time, love and patience to trust his humans, but in the right home and given time I think this boy is going to be a big, playful and lovable boy. Royal will need a home where there is already a resident dog.

Royal is a very scared boy who has come to us from a breeder. He is especially scared when it comes to being touched by us humans but when you get him in the back of the kennel he will allow you to gently stroke him but he is uncomfortable with this. At the moment Royal could possibly make the wrong decision if handled incorrectly but this is purely through fear and he is already starting to make improvements. He will actually get excited to see his kennel mum in the mornings and will wag his tail but he’s not sure how to interact with her yet.

Royal has never lived in a home so this is going to be completely overwhelming at first and he will definitely need at least one other dog in the home to help his confidence. This will help him with house training and lead walking but these are things that are going to take him time to learn as the garden may be as scary as the home at first.

Royal will need a very calm and quiet, adult only home and adopters who have lots of experience with scared dogs. We think he’ll come out of his shell a lot more over time but Royal needs a lot of TLC, time and patience.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Rowena
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have received treatment for an ear infection and am being monitored.

12-11-26 Rowena has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. She is a super sweet little lady who is still feeling worried and timid, but she is making lovely progress during her time with us. She can be particularly unsure when approached or handled and may choose to move away if she feels overwhelmed. However, she is responding well to gentle, slow handling and is coming out of her shell more and more each day. She has spooked a few times, but is doing her very best to be brave, and we are so pleased to see her confidence growing.

Rowena will be looking for a calm and quiet home where she can settle in at her own pace. She will need adopters with rescue experience, ideally with ex-breeding dogs, who understand the importance of being kind and gentle as she learns all about home life and how kind human hands can be. She is not yet at the stage where she enjoys cuddles or actively seeks out fuss, so her new family will need to give her space and allow her to build trust in her own time. If pushed beyond her comfort zone, she may panic, so patience and understanding will be essential.

Rowena relies on other dogs for comfort and confidence, so she will need a kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help show her the way. We feel that having a canine companion to follow and learn from will make a real difference to her settling in, and with this support, we hope she will continue to blossom.

Rowena has never lived in a home before, so everything will be very new to her. She will need kind and understanding adopters who can help her learn all about home life, including house training and the many little things that other dogs take for granted.

We would consider a home with dog-savvy teenagers aged 13 and over, provided they have experience of living with dogs and understand that Rowena will need her own space initially. They must be happy to let her approach them in her own time and not expect her to enjoy cuddles or attention straight away.

Rowena has received treatment for an ear infection and is being monitored.

Rowena really is a little sweetheart who is trying so hard to find her confidence. With a calm home, an understanding family and the reassurance of a kind canine companion, we hope she will continue to come out of her shell and discover all the comforts of a loving forever home.

Rowena has been given the Gift of Life by Samantha Cooper

name: Sianon
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

Sianon has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for her forever home. She is a worried girl who is unsure around humans and isn't used to being handled yet. She is going to need plenty of love, patience and TLC as she settles in and slowly begins to grow in confidence.

She has recently moved to a wonderful foster home where she is getting to experience home life for the first time and is settling in well. She is a very sweet girl who is trying so hard to be brave but is not yet comfortable being handled. She is happy to explore the home and garden but will head in the opposite direction if she sees anyone approaching. She loves her food and treats and is very interested when they appear.

Sianon will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult only home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and who understand that she will need time to adjust to her new life. Her new family will need to be kind and patient, allowing her to settle in at her own pace without putting pressure on her.

Sianon relies on other dogs for confidence, so she will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home to be her friend and help her feel safe. She loves to snuggle with the other dogs in her foster home,

She has never lived in a home before moving to foster, so everything will be new to her, and she will need gentle guidance as she learns all about home life and new skills such as house training. She doesn't yet walk on a lead and harness and will need to practice first around the home and garden until she is feeling brave enough to venture further.

Sianon is a gentle girl who has lots to learn, but with the right home, a patient family and a lovely canine friend to show her the ropes, we hope she will gradually discover her confidence and enjoy all the wonderful things life has to offer.

Sianon has been given the Gift of Life by Dee Wickson-Dix

Sianon is settling into foster. She is a sweet little girl who tries her best to be brave but is not yet comfortable at being handled. She's happy to explore the home and garden but will head in the opposite direction if she sees anyone approaching. She mixes well with all my dogs and loves to snuggle up with them. She is interested in food and will follow when she sees her dinner arriving but will wait until I leave before approaching it. She knows when the treat tin comes out and whilst she won't take a treat from me will wait for me to drop it and then quickly retrieve it.

Sianon will be looking for a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and who understand that she will need time to adjust. Her new family will need to be kind and patient, allowing her to settle in at her own pace without putting pressure on her. She has never lived in a home before, so everything will be new to her, and she will need gentle guidance as she learns all about home life and new skills such as house training and how to walk on a lead and harness.

Sianon relies on other dogs for confidence, so she will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home to be her friend and help her feel safe. We hope having a canine companion by her side will help her learn that the world isn't such a scary place. Any children in the home will need to be teenagers aged 16+.

name: Blake
description:
I would like a home filled with love and kindness!

I can be an only dog or live with other dogs. No cats please!

I would like a secure garden with 6ft+ fences.

I can walk on a lead and would love an active home.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I will need a grain free diet & I have small ear canals!

06-11-26 Blake is a wonderful, confident boy who has come into our care from a breeder and is absolutely full of beans! He is your typical happy and excitable Staffy who loves everyone he meets and is always ready to make a new friend.

Blake is confident enough that he would be happy to be homed as an only dog as long as his adopter had plenty of time to spend with him, but he does get along really well with other dogs and could be homed with a kind resident dog who won't mind his enthusiastic personality. We would consider homing him with dog savvy teenagers aged 13+ and he would be best suited to a home with adopters who have dog experience.

Blake has never lived in a home before, so his adopters will need to be patient and understanding as he learns all about home life, including house training. He will need a home with no cats or small furries.

He can walk on a lead and would love to find an active home with adopters who can keep him busy, enjoy adventures with him and understand his bouncy nature. Blake has already been showing us just how clever he can be and has recently learned to play fetch, even bringing the ball back! He even already knows how to sit on command. He is an eager-to-please boy with so much love and enthusiasm for life, and he is more than ready to find a family of his own.

We have been told the breeder that Blake requires a grain free diet, so this will need to continue in his new home. Our vet has noticed that he has narrow ear canals, but this does not seem to bother him.

Blake has been given the Gift of Life by Nicola McNamee

name: Pippa
description:
I'd like a quiet, adult-only home to help me relax and feel safe.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I will need an extra secure garden to keep me safe.

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

30-09-26 Pippa is a very scared and nervous lady who has come into our care from a breeder. She is very worried about being handled and becomes stressed if we attempt to pick her up. She will try to jump from our arms and, because of this, we would consider her a flight risk and she will need fencing of at least 6ft in her new garden to keep her safe. She will need very careful handling and adopters who understand just how frightened she is at the moment.

Pippa gets on wonderfully with her kennel friends and relies on their company for comfort, so she will need a kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help guide her and give her the reassurance she needs as she settles in and finds her paws.

As Pippa has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training and the other basics of home life. Her new family will need to be very patient and give her time to adjust to all the new sights, sounds and experiences that come with living in a home.

Pippa will need a quiet, confident, adult-only home where she can relax and settle into her new surroundings without too much hustle and bustle. Her adopters will need to have ex-breeding experience and understand her nervous nature and allow her to progress at her own pace.

Pippa is a very worried girl right now, but with the security of a kind canine companion and a calm, patient family, we hope she will slowly begin to feel safe and gain the confidence she needs to enjoy her new life.

Pippa has been given the Gift of Life by Margaret Hunter

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. name: Moxy
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult-only home.

I will need a kind, calm resident dog to show me the ropes. I'm unsure of cats.

I would like an extra-secure garden to spend time in.

I haven't tried walks just yet and will find this a bit overwhelming at the moment.

I am currently in a foster home where I am learning about home life!

Moxy is a worried little girl who has come to us from a breeder and is now in foster, where she is beginning to show her lovely, affectionate personality. She can be unsure around new people, but as she learns to trust you, more of her sweet nature shines through. In the evenings, she will come to her fosterers for a cuddle on her own terms, which is lovely to see as she continues to grow in confidence.

Moxy will need an adult-only home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and understand that she needs time, patience and kindness to settle into her new life. A calm, quiet environment with minimal disruption will be important, as will having a gentle, quiet resident dog to help her feel safe and guide her through home life. Moxy has struggled with a more vocal dog in her foster home, so her canine companion will need to be calm and considerate of her needs.

Moxy has never lived in a home before and is learning about house training and everyday routines in foster. Her new family will need to continue this patiently and gently introduce her to lead walking. She has shown signs of digging, so she will also need an extra-secure garden to keep her safe.

Moxy arrived with sore eyes, and our vet noted that her lower eyelid is irregular, although this is not currently causing her any issues. We are also concerned that her vision is significantly reduced, as her depth perception seems affected. She may bump into things or be startled when other dogs approach unexpectedly, so her adopters will need to understand her visual difficulties and help her navigate her surroundings safely. She also arrived with sore skin and old concrete sores, which we hope will continue to improve.

Moxy has already made lovely progress and is gradually learning to trust the people around her. She will need a special family who can offer a peaceful home, a calm canine companion and the understanding she needs to feel secure. With time, patience and gentle reassurance, we hope this affectionate little girl will continue to blossom and discover just how lovely life can be.

Moxy has been on our section for a few weeks now & she is such a delight to be around.

Dependent on where Moxy is will decide which side of Moxy you will get. Both sides are a truly beautiful dog, but one is incredibly sad & shut down and the other is a wonderful, affectionate girl who truly tries her hardest to be brave.

When in the kennel you’ll find Moxy in the back, she’ll appear sad, broken & totally overwhelmed. She tries to dig a lot, and burrow herself behind any beds she can find. We have swapped these beds out with a big comfy duvet now where she likes to chill in the corner. However I do think she sees it as her safe space, where she will hide from the outside world. Once she’s out of that kennel, and running to the yard she will wag her body in its entirety as she greets other kennels desperately trying to make new friends.

Even in the yard, Moxy can still feel overwhelmed and will sit in the corner & dig at times, and we’ve even tried taking her out on a harness but she remains frozen. But once she’s comfortable in the company she is around, she is the most affectionate girl. She happily sits next to you, gives you kisses and that tail really does not stop wagging. Her company is joyous, and being one of her trusted people is so incredibly rewarding, and brightens every day I spend with her.

Moxy’s people will need to take it easy with her, need to understand exbreeders, and be patient & kind along her journey at home. Mixing her nervous character along with her poor eyesight, being at home is likely to be very scary for her. As one of her kennel mummies, I can vouch for her & tell you that gaining her trust, and gaining her as a family member will be the most fulfilling experience, and one I am extremely jealous of. Moxy deserves love, care & a place to feel safe after all this time feeling scared & overwhelmed.

Moxy, like a lot of ex breeder dogs, is a very nervous dog. When I first met her, she wouldn’t leave the back, didn’t want me to get near her and I had to carry her back and forth from the yard. On my second day with Moxy, she ran straight to the yard as I opened her kennel door and, once I entered the yard, she was jumping all over me, kissing me, genuinely thrilled to see me. This is behaviour that truly shocked me in the best possible way.

It’s now been a couple of weeks since I first worked with her and the affection she shows me and the confidence she found has only grown. She’s truly incredible.Around new people, she reverts back to shutting down and hiding in the back. Despite this, we still have an incredible relationship. Moxy needs to be shown she can trust you.

Once this girl trusts you, you’ll see the same side I see. You won’t see this side if you met her on a show around of our kennels or even if you were let in her kennel to socialise her. This is something you can only experience from adopting her and progressing her like we do. I truly love her with all my heart. Take a chance on her and I have no doubts you’ll experience the same as I.

Moxy is a very worried little girl who has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. She is feeling quite overwhelmed to find herself here at the moment and is in need of lots of TLC, patience and reassurance. Once she gets to know you, she does start to come out of her shell and then enjoys a gentle fuss.

Moxy will need a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and understand that she will need plenty of time to settle in at her own pace. She will need another kind and confident resident dog in her new home to take her under their wing and help her learn how wonderful her life can be now. We would consider homing her with old, dog savvy teenagers.

Moxy has never lived in a home before, so everything will be new to her. Her new family will need to be kind and understanding as she learns all about home life, including new skills like house training and walking on a lead. She will need gentle encouragement and understanding as she settles in.

Moxy is a very sweet girl who has had a difficult start in life. She now needs someone who will give her the time, patience and love she needs to blossom. With a kind canine friend by her side and a quiet, understanding home, we hope she will slowly gain confidence and discover how lovely life can be.

Moxy has arrived with slightly sore eyes and our vet has noted her low eyelid is irregular but doesn't feel this is causing her any issues at the moment, but will need to be monitored moving forwards. Although she can see, her vision isn't the best, but she doesn't let this slow her down and gets around well. She also arrived with sore skin and old concrete sores, which will hopefully feel much better soon.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Candy
description:
I would like a home filled with love and kindness!

I can live with larger, playful resident dogs, or I can be the only dog in the home!

I would like a large, and secure garden with 6ft+ fences.

I walk well on a lead, but I can be strong so my adopters will need to work with this

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home! Read below for more!

Candy is a very sweet and affectionate lady who has come to us from a breeder and is now searching for her forever home. She absolutely adores attention and cuddles and, once she gets to know you, it doesn't take her long to show just how loving she really is. Candy simply wants to be close to her people and has completely stolen the hearts of everyone she has met. She has blossomed into the most loving girl and will make a wonderful companion and is sure to become the ultimate cuddle bug in the home.

Candy has built a lovely bond with the staff member who has worked closely with her since she first arrived. She truly trusts her and has come on so much since arriving with us. Candy has such a sweet nature and it is clear how much she enjoys spending time with people she knows and trusts.

Her lead walking has improved so much too. She is now walking much better and really enjoys her outings, although her adopters will need to continue working on her lead manners so she can enjoy plenty of adventures. She has even started joining a regular volunteer on walks. Although, she doesn't completely trust him just yet, she is beginning to learn to trust him and build a relationship.

Candy mixes well with polite, well mannered dogs however she can sometimes be a little selective with choosing her friends. She doesn’t appreciate when dogs are over the top but when she does make a new friend her own play style can be quite full on! She comes away when called so we are always able to calm her down for a tasty treat. Because of her size and excitable nature, she would not be able to live with smaller breeds of dogs in the home and will need a home without cats.

As Candy is a very large lady, it is important that her adopters have experience with a similar breed and understand her needs. We have found that she can be particularly worried by formal handling, such as veterinary examinations, and finds these situations quite stressful. We will be muzzle training Candy so that she can be safely and comfortably handled for occasions such as vet visits. She recently needed to visit the vet due to sore ears and, although she found having her ears examined uncomfortable, she coped very well with the support of people she knows and trusts. She did also need to visit the vet for a check up on a day when her regular person wasn't around and found it much harder to cope with and became extremely stressed and agitated. She takes so much comfort from her known and trusted people.

Candy would be best suited to an adult-only home where her adopters can give her the time and space she needs to build trust and settle in.

Candy has arrived with a scab on the right side of her face that will be addressed during the time of her spay and is being treated for a ear infection.

Candy has come such a long way since arriving with us and is now so ready for a loving home of her own. She is an absolute angel and a true credit to her breed, with so much love and affection to give. She truly deserves someone who will give her the love, patience and happiness she deserves.

Candy will need more than one meet and greet with her prospective adopters to allow her time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

Candy has been given the Gift of Life by Carolina Olsen

The bond I’ve built with this lovely, sweet girl is unmatched. I feel so honoured by how much trust she has given me. She really is like my best friend, and I just love spending my days with her.

Candy is such a sweet girl, but she can be wary of strangers and a little head shy, especially when new people reach over her head to give her a fuss. Whenever we're out walking and people ask to say hello, I always explain that she's head shy and ask them to let her sniff them first and approach her at her own pace. She is more than happy to take treats from people, and it's lovely to see her little interactions.

To help build her confidence with new people, Candy now goes out with one of our regular volunteers twice a week for longer walks. She doesn't trust him 100% just yet, but she'll happily go out walking with him and take treats. She's still very aware of his presence, but it's all about time, patience and allowing her to build that trust in her own time.

Candy also had her first bath with us this week! Although she wasn't too keen to begin with, she trusted me and I made sure to respect her boundaries. We managed to wash her from the shoulders down, and I'm super proud of her! The hairdryer was a definite no, but that's absolutely fine. We do everything at Candy's pace.

She's also learnt to sit, and one of her favourite things to do is play with the squeaky balls in the yard.

Candy really does feel like my best friend at the rescue. She always makes me smile, keeps me pushing through and has such a special place in my heart. I feel so lucky to have built the bond we have, and I can't wait to see her continue to grow in confidence.

Candy is an absolute angel and a true credit to her breed. I’ve worked with her since she first arrived at the rescue, and over that time we’ve built such a lovely bond. She truly trusts me and knows that I only have her best interests at heart.

Candy has blossomed into the most loving and affectionate girl, and I genuinely love spending my days with her. She has such a sweet nature and has come on so much since arriving with us.

Candy recently had a vet visit due to having sore ears. Although you could tell she was uncomfortable while the vet was examining them, she was such a good girl throughout, and I was incredibly proud of her.

She has also mixed with quite a few dogs here at the rescue and has been brilliant with all of them. She can sometimes be a little bouncy and excitable when first meeting new dogs, but she listens when asked to calm down and is learning to manage her excitement really well.

Her lead walking has improved so much too, and she’s now walking much better and enjoying her outings.

Candy has come such a long way and is so ready for a loving home of her own. She truly deserves someone who will give her the love, patience and happiness she deserves.

Candy is a very sweet and affectionate lady who has come to us from a breeder and is now searching for her forever home. She absolutely adores attention and cuddles and, once she gets to know you, it doesn't take her long to show just how loving she really is. Candy simply wants to be close to her people and has completely stolen the hearts of everyone she has met. She will make a wonderful companion and is sure to become the ultimate cuddle bug in the home.

Candy can walk on a lead, although she can be quite strong, so her adopters will need to be prepared to continue her training and help her develop her lead manners so she can enjoy plenty of adventures. As she is a very large lady, it is important that her adopters have experience with her breed and understand her needs.

Candy has the confidence to be the only dog in the home, although she could potentially live with another large breed dog following a successful meet and greet. She loves to play and can be quite excitable, so she would not be suitable to live with smaller or more fragile dogs and she will need a home without cats.

Candy is an incredible girl, but she can be sensitive when she is worried or when she feels uncomfortable, for this reason, we feel she would be best suited to an adult-only home where her adopters can give her the time and space she needs to build trust and settle in.

She has arrived with a scab on the right side of her face that will be addressed during the time of her spay.
