name: Fallon
description:
I will need an adult-only home that understands me.

I would prefer to be the only dog in the home!

I will need a secure garden, with at least 6ft+ fencing to explore!

I am new to lead walking, and would like to continue this once I have settled in.

I have lived in a home before, but may need some reminders.

I have been spayed & am ready for my forever home!

05-11-26 Fallon is a super sweet and clever girl who originally came to us from a breeder but was sadly returned after struggling to cope with visitors coming and going in her previous home. She is a sensitive lady who can find changes to her environment and unexpected interactions difficult, but she has made wonderful progress with us and has formed some lovely bonds with her main carers. Once she knows and trusts you, her silly, playful personality really starts to shine, and she gives the very best snuggles!

Fallon can mix with other dogs but would prefer to have her own space in a home, so she is looking to be the only dog. She walks well on a lead, although she can occasionally walk in circles when feeling anxious or excited. She may also bark back if another dog reacts towards her. Fallon can be sensitive when resting and has previously startled and made contact when someone sat beside her on the sofa, so her adopters will need to understand her boundaries and give her quiet, undisturbed places to relax.

Fallon is looking for an adult-only home with at least 6ft secure fencing, where her adopters have previous ex-breeding experience and a good understanding of Collies and their sensitive nature. She will need a calm environment, predictable routines and cosy bed spaces where she can retreat when she needs some quiet time.

Fallon really is a lovely girl with so much personality, and it is wonderful to see how far she has come. She just needs someone who understands her needs, respects her space and is willing to give her the time to settle. In return, they will discover a clever, playful and incredibly affectionate companion who has so much love to give!

Fallon has been given the Gift of Life by Carolina Olsen

name: Koala
description:
I can live with older children, aged 16+, who understand I need time to settle in.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I am spayed and have had 4 teeth extracted,

Koala is a worried little girl who has come to us from a breeder. When she first arrived she was very frightened and unsure of humans, but since then she has started to settle in and has started to come out of her shell. She was quite flighty and would choose to run away and hide if someone approached her.

Koala has recently moved to a wonderful foster home where she is getting to experience home life for the first time ever and is settling in well. She has a very happy, waggy tail and will even follow her fosterer around the home. She will approach her when she is sitting down, but isn't quite brave enough to accept a stroke just yet. She has settled very quickly into a routine and especially loves her food.

Koala would benefit from a calm and quiet home with adopters with experience of scared ex-breeding dogs. She could be homed witholder, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16+ who are sensible and understand that she will need plenty of space and patience.

Koala relies on other dogs for comfort and reassurance and so she will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home to be her friend and help her to settle in and learn to trust.

Koala has never lived in a home before moving to foster, so her adopters will need to be kind and understanding as she continues to learn all about home life. She has been clean in the house so far in foster. She hasn't yet started to learn about walking on a lead and harness and will need to practice once she is feeling a little braver.

Koala is a worried girl, but underneath her worries is a little lady who deserves the chance to learn how wonderful life can be. She is looking for someone special who is willing to take a chance on her and give her the time she needs to blossom.

Koala has had 4 teeth extracted at the time of her spay.

Koala has been given the Gift of Life by Margaret Hunter

Koala is a happy, waggy tailed girl. She will follow me around and approach when I'm sitting but isn't yet brave enough to accept a stroke. She is comfortable coming in and out of the house and happy to explore the various rooms. She has quickly settled into a routine and knows which is her spot for dinner. She loves her food, but is happy to share. Koala mixes well with dogs of all sizes. She has been clean in the house. Koala is looking for a home with friendly companions and with adopters who can continue to show her that hands can be kind.

Koala is a frightened little lady who has come to us from a breeder and is still very unsure of us humans. She can be quite a flighty girl and, at the moment, would much rather hide away than have people approach her. Once she is safely in your arms, she is easier to handle, but she will need plenty of time and patience to learn that people can be trusted.

Koala relies heavily on her kennel friends for confidence and comfort, so she will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home who can take her under their wing and help her feel more secure. Having a canine friend by her side will be very important as she begins to experience life outside of kennels.

Koala has never lived in a home before, so she will need understanding adopters who can give her the time she needs to settle in and learn about house training. Lead walking may be far too scary for her initially, so she will need a secure garden where she can safely explore, sniff and build her confidence at her own pace.

Koala can live with older, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16+ who are sensible and understand that she will need plenty of space and patience. Her adopters will need previous ex-breeding experience so they can better understand her needs and help her adjust to life in a home.

Koala is a very frightened girl, but underneath her worries is a little lady who deserves the chance to learn how wonderful life can be. She is looking for someone special who is willing to take a chance on her and give her the time she needs to blossom.

description:
I can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who understand I need space.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I will need a secure garden with minimum 6ft fencing.

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

Please be patient with me, I haven’t lived in a home before

Although Fanta was shaking, she allowed us to pick her up and give her a gentle fuss to reassure her that we are here to help. She is still very unsure at the moment, so her new family will need to be patient and allow her the time she needs to learn to trust.

Fanta will need another kind and confident dog in her new home, as this will be a much-needed support system for her. A reassuring canine companion can help guide her and give her the confidence she needs as she settles in and begins to find her paws.

As Fanta has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training and the other basics of home life. Her adopters will need to understand that this may take time and be prepared to let her progress at her own pace. She can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who understand she needs time to settle in. Her adopters will need to have ex-breeding experience to better understand her needs.

Fanta is a very worried little girl, but she has already shown us that she can accept gentle affection even when she is feeling frightened. We hope that with a confident canine companion, a calm environment and lots of patience, she will gradually begin to feel safe and discover the happy new life she deserves.

name: Twig
description:
I need an adult-only home where I can feel safe and loved.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I am learning about wearing a lead and harness.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

Twig has come to us from a breeder and is now searching for a loving forever home. When she first arrived, Twig was a very worried and flighty girl who found new people quite overwhelming and would often bark and keep her distance. However, after spending some time getting to know her, we have seen a lovely side to Twig that we knew was hiding underneath all those nerves.

Twig has now moved into a wonderful foster home where she is getting to experience home life for the very first time. She was very overwhelmed when she first moved into foster and would initially hide in the garden, but since then she has started to come out of her shell and is settling into home life and has started to unwind. She has started to bond with her fosterer and will now sit next to her on the sofa for snuggles but is still quite wary of her fosterers husband.

Twig relies heavily on the other dogs in her foster home for comfort and support and will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult only home where there was another kind and confident resident dog to be her friend. She will need adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and will help her settle in at her own pace.

Twig has recently started her harness training, although she is still very much at the beginning of this journey. She will need her adopters to take things slowly and give her plenty of time to build her confidence before expecting her to venture out into the big wide world. Lots of gentle practice in the garden will be a good place to start, and her adopters should be prepared to take things at her pace rather than rushing her. She is starting to learn all about toilet training and is doing well.

Twig is a sensitive girl who may take some time to fully trust her new family, but the progress she has already made shows us just how much potential she has. Once she knows you, she is such a sweet, gentle little lady who simply wants to be close to her person. She just needs someone willing to give her the time, patience and chance she deserves.

Twig has been given the Gift of Life by Carolina Olsen

Twig or 'Twiglet' as we sometimes call her came into foster with us 2 weeks ago and it's been quite an overwhelming experience for her. She started out wanting to hide in the garden and avoiding all contact with humans. It was clear she has never had any kindness prior to coming to Many Tears and learning to live in a home environment was going to be a big challenge for her.

Despite this, she has started to unwind and is heavily relying on her other dog friends for cues and support. She has slowly formed a bit of a bond with me and we've had some really lovely snuggles on the sofa but she is still wary of my husband despite him tossing occasional snacks to her from a distance. It is clear that she is just a really scared baby that desperately wants to trust people but will be a big work in progress.

We have been able to gently get a harness on her and take her to a secure field which she enjoyed but we are still working on her lead skills without her panicking.

Twig likes having dog friends to sit with on the sofa and gets on with everyone. Her toilet training is coming along and if I go for a walk in the garden she will come too and do a wee. We are still getting a few accidents overnight though which need some patience.

Twig is not going to be a ready-to-go dog and just needs someone with the patience and time to bring her out of her shell and show her the world in small stages. Once she trusts you she really is a snuggle bug!

Twig has been with me on my section for around a month now and our bond is getting stronger and stronger by the day. When she first arrived, she was quite flighty and I could tell she was very overwhelmed, and I did think she was going to be quite a difficult one to crack to begin with. Buuuuut, thankfully I was wrong!! It did take about a week or so, but one day out of nowhere she came and sat by me .. not doing anything or making any sort of gesture .. she just sat and looked at me. I very gently started stroking her under her ear and chin, expecting her to move away, but she didn’t!!! Instead, she actually came closer to me when I stopped, as if to ask for more. From then on she’s been the same with me every day. If I’m sat down in the yard or the kennel, she’s always right next to me patiently waiting for a little fuss. She never makes any noise or fuss about it, she doesn’t barge the other dogs out of the way or get jealous, she just sits there, waiting for her turn. So sweet!!!It is a bit of a different story with strangers, however. She does still bark at them and presents as a fearful and reactive dog, but as soon as she gets to know you, that all goes away. When it’s just me and her with no other people around, she’s as quiet as a mouse. So if anyone is reading this that has seen her / or maybe will see her at the rescue, please don’t take her reaction in the kennel as face value. I promise she’s a sweet angel really!This week we have started on her harness training journey. It’s still very early days yet, but it’s a marathon and not a sprint! She hasn’t taken any steps as of yet, but I’m hoping she will after a few attempts. I would definitely recommend her future adopters do lots of practice in the garden with her before venturing out into the big wide world! Slow and steady wins the race after all.Twig would really love a calm and quiet, adult only home with adopters who have experience with ex breeders and will be understanding and patient with her. It may take her a little while to learn to trust fully, but I do think she will get there. She just needs someone to give her a chance.

Twig has come to us from a breeder and is now searching for a loving forever home. She can be quite vocal when first meeting new people and prefers to keep her distance, often choosing to hide away until she feels more comfortable. However, beneath her worried exterior is a lovely little lady with a very sweet nature hiding.

Twig would love a calm and understanding home where she can settle at her own pace and begin to build her confidence. She takes great comfort from her kennel friends and will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home that she can look to for reassurance as she adjusts to family life.

Twig could live with older, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16+ who understand that she needs a quiet environment and plenty of patience. As she has never lived in a home before, her adopters will need to be understanding as she learns about house training and walking on a lead. Some gentle garden sniffs may be a good place to start while she gains confidence.

Twig is a sensitive girl who is looking for a home that can offer her plenty of love, TLC, and reassurance as she discovers that the world isn't such a scary place after all.

name: Pop
description:
I can live with older, dog-savvy kids aged 13+ who love cuddles, and are active!

I will need to be the only pet in my new home, so all of the attention is on me!

I would like a secure garden where I can have plenty of play time!

I am very active and will need a home that will take me on plenty of adventures!

I may have previously lived in a home, so I may already know the basics.

I have been spayed and am ready to find my forever home!

Pop is a fantastic little lady who has come to us from a breeder, although we have been told she has lived in a home previously. She knows her name and responds to “Pop”, so her new family will need to keep this name.

Pop is full of love, character and energy. She can be a little timid when first meeting new people, but it doesn't take her long to warm up. Once she knows you, she absolutely loves cuddles, enjoys giving kisses and thrives on human company. She has a very affectionate nature and loves being involved in whatever her people are doing.

As an active Jack Russell Terrier x Collie, Pop is looking for a home that can provide plenty of physical exercise and mental enrichment to keep her clever little brain busy. She is a quick learner who has mastered “sit” and is currently learning “touch”. She picks things up quickly, which is helping with her ongoing muzzle training.

Pop walks beautifully on her harness and would happily walk for miles, so she will need an active home that enjoys getting out and about and helping her learn new things. She is doing well with her training and is now walking alongside calm dogs, which is lovely progress. However, she is not yet comfortable wearing a muzzle for long periods, and we are continuing to build her confidence with this gradually. The aim is to help her become comfortable wearing one when needed, so she can be kept safe around other dogs in busier areas in the future. At the rescue, under supervision with her surroundings managed, she is enjoying muzzle free play time with Lassie so it is possible she will not always need a muzzle for mixing with her canine friends.

Pop will need to be the only dog in her new home. Although she is making progress with carefully managed walks alongside calm dogs, she can still become reactive when she feels overwhelmed. Her adopters will need to be experienced, understanding and committed to continuing her positive, reward-based training to help her feel more comfortable around dogs when out and about.

As Pop has previously lived in a home, we think she is likely to know many of the basics, although she may need a few reminders as she settles into a new routine. She could live with sensible, dog-savvy children aged 13 years and over but will need a home without cats.

Pop is a wonderful little dog with so much love to give. With patient, experienced adopters who can provide the active lifestyle, ongoing training and consistency she needs, she will make a fantastic, loyal and loving companion.

Pop has been making really good progress and has even made a friend here that she mixes with unmuzzled, she seems to enjoy a little bit of a play but then needs to have a little pause during some play dates when her friend gets a little bit too playful and overwhelms her. After a couple of minute of calm she will happily play again but it's important that her new people don't rush her with her socialisation, and instead, just take it at a pace that Pop is happy and comfortable with. She is very good at communicating when she's feeling a bit overwhelmed so you just have to listen to her and take her out of the stressful situation.

We are still muzzle training her to help her with her doggy social skills, this is very much a work-in-progress as we want her to be 100% happy with one step before moving on to the next, but I am very proud of her for reaching the stage of putting her nose in on queue and holding it there for a few seconds before getting more tasty paste.

In general she is such a happy ball of energy who just wants someone who will take her on adventures and truly be her best friend.

Pop can be homed with dog-savvy teens but they must be understanding of her getting a little mouthy when over-excited and although this is something that she is improving on, we don't want her new adopters to be worried by this behaviour if it were to happen in the home. We ignore it and reward her for being calm, which is all it usually takes for her to stop and then we continue with something fun, she also will usually grab a toy when excited in her kennel, so we are in the process of teaching her to do this on command to help her know where to place all that excited energy safely.

I can see her making a family incredibly happy, she really does have so much to offer the right home.

Pops is such a beautiful, smart girl who is super friendly with people. She has just mastered "sit" and is currently learning "touch". She picks things up pretty quickly, which is also helping her with her muzzle training.

Pops isn't sociable with other dogs currently, but this is something we're working on by taking her on walks with calm dogs at a distance. Once she is happily muzzle trained, we will work up to safe mixes with dogs who are a good match.

She does need to be an only dog in the home, and her people will need to keep up the training we've put in place to help her feel more comfortable around other dogs when out and about in public.

She walks absolutely beautifully on her harness and would happily walk for miles and miles, so she will need an active home who enjoys helping their dog feel happier and learn new things.

Pop is a fantastic little lady who has come to us from a breeder, although we have been told she has lived in a home previously. She knows her name and responds to "Pop", so her new family will need to keep this name.

Pop is a wonderful little girl who is full of love, character and energy. She can be a little timid when first meeting new people, but it doesn't take her long to warm up. Once she knows you, she absolutely loves cuddles, enjoys giving kisses and thrives on human company. She has a very affectionate, sweet nature and loves being involved in whatever her people are doing.

As an active Jack Russell Terrier x Collie, Pop is looking for a home that can provide plenty of physical exercise as well as mental enrichment to keep her clever little brain busy. She is doing well with her lead walking and enjoys getting out and about, but she will need owners who are committed to continuing her training and helping her build confidence.

Pop will need to be the only dog in her new home. Whilst she can walk past some dogs, she is worried by them and can become reactive on lead, making the wrong choices when she feels overwhelmed. Her adopters will need to be experienced, understanding and willing to continue working on her doggy social skills using positive, reward-based training. We have already started muzzle training with Pop to help build her confidence, with the hope that, in time, she may be able to enjoy controlled walks alongside calm canine companions.

As Pop has previously lived in a home, we think she is likely to know many of the basics, although she may need a few reminders as she settles into a new routine.

She could live with sensible, dog-savvy children aged 13 years and over but will need a home without cats.

Pop is a truly wonderful little dog with so much love to give. With patient, experienced adopters who can provide the active lifestyle and ongoing training she needs, she will make a fantastic, loyal and loving companion.

name: Bramble
description:
I could live with dog-savvy teens who respect my space.

I would like to be the only dog in my new home and cannot live with cats.

I would love a garden to run and play in!

I walk well on a lead and I would love to go on plenty of adventures!

I have lived in a home before so I may already know the basics.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

05-11-26 Bramble is a very sweet lady who originally came to us from a breeder and was adopted for a short period but sadly returned due to her reactivity with other dogs. She absolutely adores people, but she can find seeing other dogs out on walks quite overwhelming, and her reactivity stems from fear rather than anything else.

She is currently working really hard on building positive associations with other dogs and is making some lovely progress. We have found several calm dogs she is happy to walk alongside, which is a fantastic step forward! Bramble is also being muzzle trained so her future adopters can continue this training and help her feel safe when out and about, particularly in busier areas.

Bramble is looking to be the only dog in her new home, where she can have all the attention to herself without the worry of sharing her space. She can live with older, sensible and dog-savvy teenagers aged 16+ who understand her needs. She will need an extra-secure garden with fencing of at least 6ft, as well as adopters with previous experience of reactive dogs, her breed and ex-breeding dogs.

Bramble really is a lovely girl who is trying so hard to overcome her worries, and she has so much potential. She will need a family who understands that progress takes time, is happy to continue her training and can give her the patience and reassurance she deserves. We know that with the right people beside her, this special lady has so much to offer!

description:

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

08-11-26 Venus is a nervous girl who has come to us from a breeder to find her forever. She is quite overwhelmed to find herself here at the moment and clearly isn't used to humans and so is quite worried about us at the moment. Despite her fears, she will let you gently stroke her and with love and TLC we think she will start to come out of her shell.

Venus will be looking for a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and will allow her to settle in at her own pace. We would consider homing her with dog savvy teenagers.

Venus will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home who she can lean on for comfort and reassurance as she learns about the routines of home life. She has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to be understanding as she learns about house training and eventually walking on a lead. This may be too overwhelming for her at first, so she will need the opportunity to start with some gentle garden exploring and sniffing while she gets used to her new surroundings.

Venus is a timid girl who will need a special home willing to give her the time and patience she deserves. With a kind family and a confident doggy friend by her side, we hope she can slowly find her paws and discover how lovely life in a home can be.

Venus has been given the Gift of Life by Julie Way

name: Dora
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog in my new home who is my size or larger.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I can walk on a lead and harness and love to explore quiet areas.

I have spent some time in a home so may know the basics.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

Dora is a very worried little girl who originally came to us from a breeder. She spent around 10 months with us before being adopted, but sadly, after only a few months with her adopters, Dora returned to us due to a change in their circumstances.

Unfortunately, Dora has not been dealt the easiest set of cards, but she continues to prove just how brave and strong she is. Despite all the recent changes, she is making new kennel friends, recognising familiar staff members and allowing gentle, slow pets. Dora has made some lovely progress, and it is wonderful to see her continuing to find her feet.

Dora will need a calm and quiet, adult-only home with adopters who have experience with very scared ex-breeding dogs. She relies heavily on other dogs for confidence and comfort, so she will need a kind and confident resident dog, preferably her size or larger, to be her friend and help show her the ropes.

Having previously lived in a home, Dora has made some lovely progress, but moving somewhere new will still be a big change. She will need plenty of time, patience and TLC to settle and may need some gentle reminders about her house training.

Dora will now allow gentle strokes, provided you take things slowly and give her the choice to approach. She is still very unsure of handling and does not enjoy being picked up or having her harness put on or taken off. She is very food motivated, however, and will happily come over for some tasty paste! Once wearing her harness, she can walk nicely on a lead.

Dora is looking for a very special home where she can continue to build her confidence and learn to trust the people around her. Perhaps, in time, handling will become less frightening for her, or perhaps she may never fully feel comfortable with it. Either way, she deserves a family who will give her the patience, love and understanding she needs and accept her just as she is.

Even with all the recent changes, she is making new kennel friends, recognising familiar staff members and allowing gentle, slow pets.

I really hope Dora finds a home filled with love, patience and understanding, where she can continue to build her confidence and learn that handling doesn't have to be such a scary thing. Or perhaps she may never fully feel comfortable with handling, and that's okay too. We hope her future family will love and accept her just as she is, quirks and all.

name: Rizzle
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I have been spayed & am ready for my forever home!

Rizzle is a quiet and timid girl who has come to us from a breeder. When she arrived she was quite overwhelmed and in need of plenty of TLC, but she has since started to come out of her shell.

Rizzle has recently moved to a wonderful foster home where she is settling in and starting to learn about home life for the first time ever. She is making gentle progress and is even starting to wag her tail when her fosterer speaks to her and has ventured onto the sofa twice so far, although she is understandably still quite nervous and isn't yet feeling brave enough to approach but is trying her hardest to be brave.

She will be looking for a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and who will allow her to settle in at her own pace. She will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home who she can look to and lean on as she begins to gain confidence and learns that the world isn’t such a scary place.

She has never lived in a home before moving to foster, so her adopters will need to be kind and patient as she learns all about home life, including house training, though she is starting to get to grips with this already. She doesn't yet walk on a lead and harness as she is quite worried about being handled, but hopefully this will be introduced to her in the near future.

She is a sweet little lady with so much potential and just needs someone willing to take a chance on her. With a loving home, a confident canine companion and plenty of patience, we’re sure Rizzle will slowly find her confidence and become a wonderful companion.

Rizzle has been given the Gift of Life by Carolina Olsen

Rizzle is a real sweetheart, but still very nervous, moving away from me most of the time. She has just started to wag her tail when I talk to her and has twice shared the sofa, but at a distance. If she moves into a corner, I can give her a brief stroke, otherwise she will only come for a quick sniff of my hand. She is not yet confident enough to take a treat from me. She eats well, preferring to eat alone, but not because of any guarding issues.

Rizzle has chewed toys and played with Petal, my other foster dog, but this is not a regular occurrence. She spends a lot of time alongside Petal. She is getting used to household sounds, dislikes the vacuum cleaner and goes in the garden but is OK with the washing machine, and tolerates the ironing board.

Rizzle will briefly bark if she hears a sound in the garden, eg another dog or voices. At night or if I go out, she sleeps quietly in the lounge with the other dogs. She doesn't enjoy handling at the moment, so I have not made any attempt to put a harness on her. Her toilet training is a work in progress, being clean when the back door is open.

Rizzle is a quiet and timid girl who has come to us from a breeder. She is beginning to show us just how inquisitive she can be and is trying her hardest to be brave. Rizzle isn’t quite ready to approach us just yet, but she does follow the lead of her doggy friends and takes lots of comfort from having them around. With plenty of TLC, patience and reassurance, we’re sure it shouldn’t take her too long to come around and start showing her lovely personality.

Rizzle will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home who she can look to and lean on as she begins to gain confidence and learns that the world isn’t such a scary place. She has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to be kind and patient as she learns all about home life, including house training. She will need time to take everything at her own pace and shouldn’t be rushed before she is ready.

Rizzle can live with older, dog-savvy children who are sensible and will understand that she needs time and space to settle in. She is a sweet little lady with so much potential and just needs someone willing to take a chance on her. With a loving home, a confident canine companion and plenty of patience, we’re sure Rizzle will slowly find her confidence and become a wonderful companion.

name: Kirk
description:
I can live with older, dog savvy teenagers, aged 13+ who respect my space.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

30-09-26 Kirk is a scared young lad who has come into our care from a breeder. He is not used to being handled, but he will accept us picking him up and, once he is settled in our arms, he seems to really enjoy a gentle fuss.

Kirk is currently kennelled with another male dog, but we think he would be fine to be homed with a suitable female too. We believe that Kirk will need another dog in his new home, and this canine companion will be a much-needed support system for him as he settles in and begins to find his confidence.

As Kirk has never lived in a home before, he will need to learn all about house training, lead training and the other basics of home life. His new family will need to be patient and understanding while he gets used to all the new experiences that come with living in a home. He can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged 13+ who are sensible.

Kirk has arrived with matted fur, so he will be having a much-needed groom to help him feel more comfortable and start to feel a little more like himself.

Kirk is a sweet young boy who is understandably unsure at the moment, but we can already see that he enjoys affection once he feels safe. We hope that with the support of a kind canine companion, a patient family and plenty of TLC, he will slowly grow in confidence and enjoy the happy new start he deserves.

Our vets have noted that Kirk has an enlarged prostate, which the vet suspects is due to benign prostatic hyperplasia. This can cause him to dribble urine and his urinary signs will need to be monitored, and further investigation or treatment may be required if these persist or do not improve. Our vets have also noted he has a small penis compared to his prepuce, which could contribute to this.

Kirk has been given the Gift of Life by Margaret Hunter

name: Cooper
description:
I would like a calm and quiet, adult only home in a semi-rural area.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I don't mind cats!

I would love a good sized garden to explore and will need 6ft fences.

I am a beginner to walking on a lead, but would like an active home.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am neutered and ready to find my forever home! Read below for more!

Meet Cooper, a lovely boy who has travelled all the way from Romania to begin his new life and search for his forever home. He is a sweet boy who was extremely overwhelmed when he first arrived. Although he is still feeling quite overwhelmed to find himself here and can be very worried, especially in new situations, he is making good progress, especially with those people he knows. He was initially very worried when he first met new people, but his circle of friends has grown and he is making more human friends daily. With his favourite people, he is a friendly, affectionate boy.

Cooper will be looking for a home with adopters with experience of scared rescue dogs and though not essential, experience with Romanian rescue dogs would be a bonus. He would be happiest in a calm, quiet, adult only home where he can settle in at his own pace and continue building his confidence. Cooper would be best suited to a home in a rural or semi-rural location and would prefer to go for walks in quiet areas. He will need a secure garden with 6ft fences.

Cooper is especially worried when he finds himself in new or unfamiliar areas, and busy environments with lots of noise, people and hustle and bustle can feel particularly overwhelming for him. He finds visiting the front of the rescue and reception area quite daunting, where there is more activity and unfamiliar sights and sounds. However, when he is given the chance to spend time in a quieter, open yard, he is much more relaxed and happy, showing us that he does best when he has space and a calm environment around him.

Cooper absolutely adores other dogs and takes great comfort from having canine friends around him, so he will need another kind, confident and playful resident dog in his new home to be his companion and show him the ropes. He is also beginning to discover the joy of toys and is enjoying learning how to play, which is so sweet. He has met cats at the rescue fine, and we may consider homing him with a dog-savvy cat.

As Cooper has never lived in a home before, his adopters will need to be patient, kind and understanding while he settles in and learns all about home life, including new skills like house training. He is very much a beginner when it comes to walking on a lead and harness, but he is already starting to enjoy his walks and would love an active home where he can continue exploring the world at his own pace.

With patience, understanding and plenty of love, Cooper will start to discover just how wonderful his life can now be. In return, this gentle boy will reward his family with the privilege of watching him blossom into the happy and loved companion he was always meant to be. He will require multiple meet and greets with his potential adopters to give him plenty of time to get comfortable with his new family.

He is currently being monitored for left back leg lameness, and has a potential soft tissue injury. He will continue to be monitored by our vets for any further treatment he may need.

He has tested negative prior to arrival for heartworm, lyme disease, ehrlichia, anaplasma, giardia, leishmania and brucellosis.

It’s been just over a month since I last did an update on our handsome boy Cooper and since then his confidence has grown even more!

Cooper is now the centre of attention in our big play group, he will engage in play with all the dogs who attend, and even greet any new ones with very good manners! Cooper is also now making lots of human friends with numerous members of staff that he used to be scared of!!

It’s absolutely crazy to see how confident Cooper is being, compared to the day he first arrived! It just goes to show all it take is time, patience and love!

I literally love Cooper with all my heart, watching him turn into the happiest, friendliest boy makes my heart so full!

I really hope his time to be in a home comes soon, he really does have so much love to give when he knows you!

When Cooper first arrived, his world was filled with fear. He would quietly tuck himself away at the back of his kennel, very unsure of all his surroundings and who we all were. It was so heartbreaking to see how scared cooper really was.

But every day, with kindness, patience and love, Cooper has taken another tiny step forward. Those tiny steps have turned into giant leaps. Today, the Cooper who once hid away greets his kennel mum with a wagging tail every morning and spends his days happily playing or relaxing with his kennel friends. His personality is really staring to come through and he is slowly learning that the world isn't such a scary place.

When Cooper first arrived, he'd had very little experience walking on a lead. Now he is improving so much more, he even happily takes trips down to our big play yard!

Cooper still finds unfamiliar places and new people a little scary, but it doesn't take long for him to realise he's safe. Once he trusts you, you see the sweetest, gentlest soul who simply wants to love and be loved.

Cooper has done everything we've asked of him. He's been brave. He's learned to trust. He's opened his heart. Now, we're asking for someone to do the same for him.

This beautiful young boy shouldn't be growing up behind kennel doors. He should be learning about the world from the comfort of a sofa, chasing toys around a garden, falling asleep after long walks, and knowing what it feels like to be in a home.

I am so incredibly proud of the progress Cooper has made and I have no doubts in a home with all the patience and kindness he will blossom into the most amazing loving family member anyone could wish for.

name: Hatty
description:
I need an experienced adult-only home where I can feel safe and loved.

I need a resident dog to help me feel safe. I've never met cats so I'm unsure!

I'm a bit of a Houdini and will need a secure garden to keep me safe.

I am too scared to go out for walks right now and will need careful introduction.

I'm still learning house training, lead walking, and other basics of home life.

I’m fully vaccinated and spayed, ready for my forever home!

30-09-26 Hatty originally came to us from a breeder, and was adopted for a period of time, and was sadly returned to our care due to her adopter becoming unwell. She managed a recent vet visit incredibly well considering how worried she can be, allowing the vet to examine her and administer her vaccinations while she was safely cuddled in her blanket. We know that the right home for Hatty is out there, and that with someone who truly understands her, she can form an incredibly special bond.Hatty is a very worried little lady who has come such a long way since arriving with us. She finds human interaction incredibly stressful and can still be very timid and defensive when she feels she is going to be handled. However, she has made some lovely progress in her foster home and is showing us that, with the right person and plenty of patience, she can learn to feel safe.

Hatty will still need a blanket to help her feel comfortable when she needs to be picked up, and she can become frightened enough to toilet herself when she is worried about being handled. Once she is safely settled, she will allow gentle strokes around her face, head and back, although she is not comfortable with her feet being touched. Her foster home has found that she is happiest when she is given plenty of space and allowed to approach things at her own pace.

Hatty absolutely loves other dogs and is particularly happy around other Dachshunds. She gets very excited to see her dog friends and enjoys being around them, so she will need a confident resident dog in her new home who can help her feel safe and show her the ropes. She enjoys having a cosy space of her own to retreat to, but also loves being able to relax on the sofa alongside the other dogs.

Hatty is very treat motivated and will happily come over for treats, which is a lovely way for her adopters to build a positive relationship with her. She is content plodding around, observing what is going on and enjoying the company of her canine friends. She can be destructive if left alone, so her adopters will need to be prepared for this and ensure she has plenty of safe things to occupy her.

Hatty will need a very special home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and understand just how frightening the world can feel for her. She will need a quiet, adult-only home with someone who is around most of the time and who can give her the time and space she needs without placing expectations on her. She will need gentle handling and continued support with things such as toilet training and lead training, although walks may not be something she becomes comfortable with.

Hatty is not going to be an easy dog to rehome, but she is a very special and frightened girl who deserves someone willing to see past her worries. With a confident canine companion, a quiet home and an adopter who can give her the time and patience she needs, we believe Hatty can continue to flourish and discover just how lovely life can be.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Juice
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I have learned how to walk on a lead and am enjoying going for walks.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I have had 7 teeth extracted at the time of my spay.

Juice came to us from a breeder and when she first arrived, she was understandably very shy and overwhelmed by everything around her. She wanted to trust people but was nervous about approaching, often hovering nearby and watching with interest before her worries got the better of her. She has since moved into foster and has made some lovely progress and is settling in well. Juice is still cautious, but she now follows her fosterers around the house and will approach for fuss when they offer their hand to her. She particularly loves belly rubs and will completely relax and close her eyes!

Juice will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult only home with adopters who have experience with scared ex-breeding dogs and who will allow her to settle in at her own pace. She will need another kind and confident resident dog in her new home who can take her under their wing and help her settle into her new home. Although she does rely on other dogs for comfort, she can guard her bed from other dogs, particularly when she has just woken up, so she will need a calm, relaxed resident dog who will not disturb her while she is sleeping. She can also be startled by people when she is in her bed and on one occasion she did nip her fosterer when they stroked her in her bed. Her new family will therefore need to be confident managing this behaviour, recognising her body language and ensuring she is always left undisturbed when she is resting.

Juice had never lived in a home before moving to foster, but she is already settling in wonderfully. Her toilet training is going really well and she has only had 2 accidents in the home so far. She has also learned all about walking on a lead and harness and is now becoming more confident wearing her harness and she is starting to enjoy her walks. She is also beginning to understand that the home is a safe place, happily relaxing and sleeping near her fosterers and enjoying the company of their resident dog.

Juice will be looking for an adult-only home with experienced adopters who understand that she is still learning to trust and who will allow her to continue building her confidence at her own pace. She has already come such a long way in a short time, and we hope that with the right family, she will continue to blossom into a happy and loving companion.

She has had 7 teeth extracted at the time of her spay.

Juice has been given the Gift of Life by Holly Kantolinna

Juice has settled in really well. She is still cautious but follows us around the house although backs off if we approach her as she prefers it if you put your hand out to her. She will then approach us, sniff our hand and accept fuss and scratches. She loves having scratches but her favourite are belly rubs and she will close her eyes and completely relax!

She sleeps well over night in her bed on the floor in our bedroom and will wake us up by walking around the room when she needs to go to toilet. Her toilet training is going really well and apart from 2 accidents early on she goes in the garden either asking to go out or when the back door is open taking herself out to go.

She is getting more confident having her harness on for walk and as long as you put it on slowly, she is happy to have it on. She is starting to walk really well on her lead and enjoys her walks and plenty of sniffs! She has met a few dogs on her walks and as long as they are not too energetic and boisterous she seems happy to meet them and have a sniff! She is ok walking along roads but does startle if there are any loud or sudden noises.

She loves being with us in the house and although she doesn't sit right next to us she enjoys being close by and really relaxes and sleeps. She enjoys being with our resident dog but is also happy to follow us outside or sit with us when our dog isn't there. She's also happy travelling in the car with our dog.

She hasn't mastered going up and down stairs yet so at present we are carrying her up and down. She is starting to go up a few small steps on her walks.

She enjoys her food and will sometimes take treats or food from our hands.  She is a lovely girl who has really progressed in the short time that we have had her and is continuing to develop her confidence.

Juice will need an experienced, adult only home with adopters who can understand and manage her nervousness and recognise when she needs space. She can guard her bed from other dogs, particularly when she has just woken up, so any resident dog will need to be calm and relaxed and not likely to bother her while she is sleeping. She can also be startled by people when she is in her bed and, on one occasion, she did nip when she was stroked resting. Her adopters will therefore need to be confident in managing this behaviour, ensuring she is left undisturbed in her bed and giving her the space she needs to feel safe and comfortable.

Juice has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for a loving forever home where she can begin the next chapter of her life.

She is a wonderful little lady who is feeling a little shy and overwhelmed at the moment, but she is trying so hard to be brave. Juice is already showing lovely signs that she wants to trust people. She will quietly hover nearby, watching you with interest and looking as though she would really like to come over for a gentle fuss, but at the last moment her worries get the better of her. We think that with time, patience, love and plenty of reassurance, her confidence will continue to grow and her true personality will begin to shine through.

Juice will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult only home where she can settle in at her own pace. She will need patient adopters who understand that building trust takes time and who will let her make progress without putting any pressure on her. She will also need another kind and confident resident dog in her new home who can be her friend and help show her that life is full of good things.

As Juice has never lived in a home before, everything will be a brand new experience for her. She will need help with housetraining, learning about household routines and gradually becoming accustomed to all the sights and sounds of family life. She is also yet to learn how to walk on a lead and harness, so her adopters will need to introduce this gently and positively as her confidence grows.

Juice is a lovely girl with so much potential. With a patient family by her side and a canine friend to guide her, we are sure she will blossom into a happy and much-loved companion.

name: Lollipop
description:
I could live with dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 +, who respect my space.

I need a doggy friend in my new home and would prefer a male dog. I don't mind cats!

I'm new to lead walking and need some practice!

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I have a grade 2 luxating patella and have had 7 teeth extracted. Read below for more

Lollipop is a lovely Bichon Frise who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start. She is an inquisitive and funny little girl who is already showing glimpses of her playful personality. Lollipop will happily come over to lick our fingers before darting away again, as if she's still deciding whether people are quite as interesting as her kennel friends.

Lollipop is still a nervous little girl, but she has been making lovely progress and is gradually becoming more curious about the people around her. The more time you spend with her, the more interested she becomes in you, and it is lovely to see her slowly coming out of her shell.

Lollipop loves the company of other dogs and relies heavily on them for comfort and reassurance. She is happy to follow their lead and takes great confidence from having another dog around. For this reason, she will need to have a resident dog in her new home. She will be looking for a home with a male resident dog as she can sometimes be a little sassy with female dogs.

Lollipop has also been making lovely progress with her harness training. She is easy to put her harness on and recently went out for her very first walk. Considering how nervous she can be, she did incredibly well! She will need plenty more gentle practice to help her become confident and comfortable with walking, and her adopters will need to continue this at her own pace.

As Lollipop has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training and the other basics of home life. Her adopters will need to be patient and understanding as she adjusts to a whole new world and gains confidence in her surroundings.

Lollipop could share her home with older, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 and over who can appreciate and understand that she will need a gentle, quiet introduction to the home and her own space to settle in.

She has arrived with a Grade 2 luxating patella, but her mobility appears unaffected and this may improve as she builds muscle tone. Lollipop has also arrived with severe periodontal disease and has had seven teeth extracted.

Lollipop is an active and spritely little girl with a bright future ahead of her. With the support of a kind canine friend and a patient family, we hope her confidence will continue to grow and her charming personality will shine through even more.

Lollipop has been given the Gift of Life by Jodie Stanley

Lollipop is a lovely lady, she’s doing ever so well here and making great progress in confidence. She loves going out for a stroll or bouncing around with her friends in our yards. Lollipop also loves to sunbath as seen in her photos.

Lollipop still has a way to go in terms of confidence with humans and is looking for a gentle adult only home with where there will be a doggie (male as she can be a little sassy with female dogs)  companion. Lollipop really is a sweet, funny and  gentle lady, and so ready for a proper home.

Lollipop has been making lovely progress with her harness training. Today, she went out for her very first walk and, considering she is still quite a nervous girl, she did incredibly well. She is easy to put her harness on, but she will need plenty more practice to help her become confident and comfortable with walking.

Lollipop relies heavily on her kennel friends for reassurance, so she will need a kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help her settle into family life. The more time you spend with her, the more curious she becomes about you, and it is lovely to see her gradually coming out of her shell.

She definitely prefers the company of other dogs at the moment, but she is happy to follow their lead and takes great comfort from having them around. As Lollipop gets on wonderfully with her kennel friends, she will need a kind resident dog in her new home to help guide her and give her the reassurance she needs as she settles in and finds her paws.

As Lollipop has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training, and the other basics of home life. Her adopters will need to be patient and understanding as she adjusts to a whole new world and gains confidence in her surroundings.

Lollipop could share her home with older dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 and over who can appreciate and understand that she will need a gentle, quiet introduction to the home and her own space to settle in.

She has arrived with a Grade 2 luxating patella but her mobility appears unaffected and this may improve as she builds muscle tone. Lollipop has also arrived with severe periodontal disease and has had 7 teeth extracted.

Lollipop is an active and spritely little girl with a bright future ahead of her. With the support of a canine friend and a patient family, we hope her confidence will continue to grow and her charming personality will shine through even more.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Faith
description:
I will need an adult-only home that understands I need time to settle in.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I will need a large, extra-secure garden to keep me safe as I learn about the home.

I’m new to walking on a harness and doing well!

Please be patient with me, I haven’t lived in a home before.

I've started my vaccinations and will be spayed before adoption.

Faith is a beautiful girl who came to us from a breeder and was initially incredibly shut down and terrified of people. She would run away from any human interaction and wouldn't even eat when people were around. However, over the last two months, Faith has made some wonderful progress and is slowly learning that people can be kind. She now walks on a harness, although she can still be easily spooked, and is happiest walking with people she knows and trusts. She will now take treats from us in her kennel, and sometimes on walks when things are quiet, with hot dogs being a particular favourite! Recently, she even allowed a little gentle fuss in the big play yard, choosing to stay for affection rather than run away. This may seem like a small step, but for Faith, it is a huge achievement.

Faith absolutely adores other dogs and truly comes alive when joining her friends for playtime in our big yard. She approaches them with a full-body wiggle and has even discovered how much fun toys can be, although she cannot be left unsupervised with soft toys! She will need a kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help her continue building her confidence and show her the ropes of home life. As a Collie, she will also need plenty of enrichment and exercise to keep her busy once she has settled in.

Faith is still a very nervous girl who will need an adult-only home with Collie experience, where her progress will be celebrated and she can continue learning at her own pace. She has never lived in a home before, so she will need patient adopters who can help her with house training, lead walking and all the other new experiences that come with family life. She will also need an extra-secure garden of at least 6ft to keep her safe as she settles in.

Faith really is such a sweet girl who tries her very hardest to be brave. Although she is making lovely progress with us, kennels is no place for a puppy to spend these important months of her life. Her three Collie friends who arrived with her have all found their forever homes, and now it is Faith's turn to find someone who can see just how far she has come and how much potential she has. With time, patience and lots of love, we know this special girl has so much more to discover, and we desperately hope her forever family won't keep her waiting much longer.

Faith has been given the Gift of Life by Raychel Mount

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Lassie
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog Cocker Spaniel size or larger in my new home. No cats please!

I would like a secure garden with 6ft boundariesto spend time in.

I can walk well on a lead and would love an active home.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have been spayed and am ready for my forever home.

Lassie has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. When she first arrived she was overwhelmed by absolutely everything, especially people. She had very little trust in humans in general which meant her kennel humans had to put in a lot of time and effort in to gaining her trust and helping her grow her circle. When meeting new people she needs to put distance between her and them until she decides that she is comfortable enough to approach them. If the person was to make Lassie feel trapped then she may growl or bark to ask for distance.

Once she has a bond with you she becomes the most affectionate, attentive, loyal and loving dog to have as a companion. Lassie will need a resident dog in her new home and since arriving she has had a variety of kennel friends, including a Bernese, Pomskis, Collie, and Beagle. She is also yarded with a mixture of other dogs and does well with them all. She does seem to prefer Collies and would love a Collie friend in her new home, but she could be homed with any dog that is no smaller than a Cocker, as she does find little dogs very fun to herd.

Due to Lassie’s past she is looking for a home with no cats, small furries or livestock and adopters who will never let her off lead anywhere near sheep fields as she is fixated with them, not surprisingly due to her breed. Lassie must always be kept safe from making the wrong decisions.

Lassie has never lived in a home before so her adopters will need to be kind and understanding as she settles in and learns all about home life as well as new skills like house training.

In the right home Lassie will thrive. She doesn't cope well in busy environments, so someone who enjoys quiet country walks with her would be a great fit.  Things like busy cafes and pubs would be far too much for her at the moment and she may never enjoy those things, so her prospective new family will need to bare that in mind when considering bringing her into their home.

Lassie is a very smart girl who does pick up new things quickly when in a calm and stress free environment. She has learnt 'sit', 'down' and is currently learning 'touch'. She also sits beautifully on the grass verge when waiting for cars to go past on her walks. Walks really are her favourite thing, whenever her harness comes out her whole body can't help but wag but can still be startled by traffic and loud noises.

She is a girl who does require patience and understanding, especially in the beginning, but she gives you so much in return and will make someone very lucky indeed.

Lassie will need more than one meet and greet with her prospective adopters to allow her time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

Lassie has been in foster for a week now and is making lovely progress every day! She is still a nervous girl who startles easily, but she is beginning to come out of her shell and will now approach her foster family for fuss. She absolutely loves belly rubs and greets them each morning with a lovely waggy tail!

She gets on brilliantly with the three resident dogs, enjoying running around and playing ball with her new friends. Lassie is also learning all about house training and is doing well. She loves her food and treats, sleeps quietly through the night in her bedroom crate with the door open, and is a wonderful passenger in the car. She happily jumps in and out and enjoys watching the world go by through the window.

Lassie walks well on the lead but can still be startled by traffic and loud noises, so she will need patient adopters who understand nervous Collies and can help her build confidence at her own pace.

Lassie will need a secure garden and a kind, confident resident dog to help her feel safe. She is looking for a home without children or cats, where she can continue to blossom with time, patience and understanding.

Lassie has proved to us, once Lassie knows and trusts you, she will be a friend for life.

Lassie is doing absolutely amazing at making doggy friends lately. She has been socialising with Cockers, Springer crosses, a large Cav, and her kennel friend is a Pomsky now. To start, she is a bit wary but does settle okay if they're not too in her face and allow her to just exist around them for a while. She's the most affectionate girl when she knows you well, but bonding with new people is a slow process, and her new people will really need to understand all of her quirks and be willing to put in the time to help her trust them.

Lassie walks well with her trusted people and will happily walk for miles and miles. She will also settle in her chosen human's presence well, and she does know how to relax here in kennels too.

I cannot express how much I adore this girl, and the loyalty and love she gives you once you've earned a spot in her trusted circle is beyond anything I can begin to describe. She's just incredible.

I took Lassie off-site to the Black Mountain Range. Kennels are no place for an energetic collie, so we set off on a 6.5km hike.

We set off, and the first thing that surprised me was how well she settled in the car. She was good as gold. Quietly and calmly sat still, occasionally getting up to look through the window. Given she is your standard high-energy collie, and the energy she exerts in kennels, I expected her to be majorly fidgety and unsettled. Boy, was I wrong, perfect passenger princess.

Once we began the hike, she instantly diverted to sniffs. Obviously, I allow her all the sniffs she wants. A 2-year-old collie that has been with us over a year, of course I want her to experience all these new scents she’s never smelt before!

Along the way, she decided she wanted to frolic and roll in some wildflowers, so naturally I joined her. We stopped, had a 5 min rest, some water and treats, before continuing.

Not far after, we encountered some sheep. Lassie did indeed stalk the sheep. She was double-leaded at all times, so this was not an issue. It must be said, Lassie is not a dog that should be off-lead right now. She can definitely be a flight risk and, if she starts herding sheep on farmers' land...

On the way back down, we ran for about 1.5km. She thoroughly enjoyed this!

She was the perfect hiking companion. All in all, 6.5km hike with 400m elevation in 1h15mins, and she was just as full of energy at the end as she was to begin. Safe to say, collies NEED that daily opportunity to alleviate some of that “crazy collie energy”!

I gave her paws a quick clean, gave her a dental stick for the journey home (it didn’t last 1/4 of the way back), and we returned to the rescue for dinner. Successful outing with the most incredible collie!

Lassie spent some time in the office today and coped really well. She happily tucked into a chicken foot for a tasty treat, although she couldn't resist pinching her kennel friend's one too! She was very curious about everything going on around her and enjoyed exploring her surroundings.

A member of staff she hadn't met before came into the office, and although Lassie was a little wary at first, she quickly settled and went back to happily enjoying her chicken foot. It was lovely to see her take the new experience in her stride and continue growing in confidence.

Beautiful beautiful Lassie! What a collie she is, she is so bright and has really come on so much with her basic training. Now knowing "sit" and "lie down". When we're out walking and a car is approaching, all I have to do is ask her to the verge and she sits and waits beautifully until we're able to start walking again. She really doesn't seem to be fazed by much traffic, but is very fixated with sheep if she comes across any. She passes horses lovely and will happily walk past other dogs no issue, but isn't keen on them approaching her. She's a big fan of food which helps with her training.She just needs people that understand that the girl she is when they first meet her is very worried but once she trusts you, her true personality really shines through.

Lassie is such a pretty girl who would do anything for you when she trusts you but is still wary of people initially. She did take treats off of a new person yesterday which was amazing to see. She needs to be in a collie experienced home with someone who will allow her the time to trust them at her own pace. She does love having a playfriend and she seems to be happiest when amongst other collies and collie crosses. She doesn't like sharing her food but is happy to share toys, beds and treats.

Lassie absolutely loves going out for her walks and gets very excited when she knows it’s time to head out. She really enjoys having a good sniff along the way and is always very interested in watching what’s going on in the fields as she passes by. Once she gets to know you, she is incredibly loving and affectionate, although she can take a little bit of time to warm up to new people. Lassie would still need a home with a resident dog, and she would truly thrive in a collie-experienced home where her needs and personality can be well understood.

Lassie is such a beautiful girl and once she knows you, she is the most affectionate, loyal and loving companion. She now walks well on a lead and absolutely loves her walks.

She will need a home with at least one other kind and confident resident dog who is a similar size to her and who loves to have a good play sometimes.

She doesn't like to share her food bowl, so he will need to be fed separately and this is something that her adopters will need to manage. In the right home she'll be someone's absolute best friend.

Lassie is a worried little lady who has come to us from a breeder. She has not had much experience with people, so everything feels very new and overwhelming to her. She can be quite skittish when approached, so she will need a calm, experienced home where she can be given the time and patience she needs to learn to trust.

At the moment, Lassie is scared of being touched, but she has already started to build a bond with her kennel mum and now allows gentle strokes from her. This shows that with consistency and kindness, shecanlearn to trust, and once she feels safe, she will begin to show her sweet side.

Lassie does walk on a lead, though she finds new experiences worrying, so she will need gentle introductions to the big wide world. She will also need to learn about house training and all the basics of living in a home, as these are things she has never known before.

Because Lassie is such a sensitive soul, she will need an adult-only home with no visiting children, and adopters who are happy to take things slowly at her pace. She will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home who can help her feel secure and show her the ropes. She gets on brilliantly with all dogs here and socialises well with a variety of breeds and sizes. She cannot be homed with cats or small furries.

With time, patience, and lots of love, Lassie will blossom. Once she has settled and gained confidence, she will become a cracking addition to her new family and will enjoy all the adventures life has to offer.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Gabriel
description:
I need an adult-only experienced home that understands me.

I would need to be the only animal in the home.

I may be shy now, but once I have settled I would love a nice garden I can play in!

I love going for walks, and would love an active home!

I know some tricks & walk well on the lead but will need help with housetraining.

I have been neutered and am ready to find my forever home.

Gabriel originally came to us from a breeder, and for him the world felt like a very frightening place. He was worried of people, and new environments and unfamiliar experiences left him feeling overwhelmed. Even something as simple as having a lead put on was a huge challenge. He needed time, patience and gentle encouragement to begin to feel safe.

Gabriel was adopted for a short period, but unfortunately it was not the right fit for him. He was returned after displaying unwanted behaviours in the home and making the wrong choices when he felt uncomfortable in a situation, which did result in Gabriel biting. He will need a quiet, adult-only home without resident or visiting children. Gabriel can struggle with visitors coming to the house, so he will need a home without too many visitors and where he can be placed in a separate room when people do come over. His adopters will also need to be willing to meet him multiple times before adoption so that he has the opportunity to develop a bond and build trust with them.

Gabriel is a very sensitive boy who feels anxious about a lot of things. During his time here we are trying to help him feel more comfortable by giving him the tools to know how to be more relaxed in these scary situations. To Gabriel, new people are very scary and he feels that he needs to tell them to go away by barking and lunging, when put in poor situations this has led to him having a bite history. He is a very sweet dog but he has very little he trusts in this world and unfortunately humans are top of that list at the moment. With people who have earned his trust he is exceptionally sweet and loving, he loves to give you cuddles and he really thinks he should be a lap dog. When introductions are done slowly and in a manner that he can cope with he will allow that person into his circle reasonably quickly and then he gets very excited to see them.

As he has had very little in this world he does become exceptionally attached to his trusted humans and doesn't like to share them with other dogs or other people, so he is looking for a home with a maximum of two people and will need to be the only dog in the home. Adopters with experience of guarding behaviours are essential to help him succeed in his next home and make sure it really will be his forever home.

Gabriel walks nicely on his harness and gets very excited to see dogs when out and about but is wary of strangers walking past, for this reason he is muzzled when out as it keeps him safe in the event of someone getting too close or trying to touch him.

He has shown signs of resource guarding his food here and any high value long lasting treats. He has Kongs as he is happy for the empty Kong to be removed from his kennel once he feels he's finished with it, but these are things that will have to be managed in his new home. It would be a good idea to limit his access to the kitchen in the home to avoid the possibility of him getting things that he may be inclined to guard, especially until he settles and the bond has been built with him to ensure that he trusts that you won't take things away from him without him getting something higher value in its place.

Gabriel socialises well with other dogs here and does enjoy chasing dogs around our big play yard here, so having the opportunity to continue making friends with playful dogs in his new home is necessary to keep him happy and help him to continue to grow in confidence. Someone will be incredibly lucky to have Gabriel as their companion, they will just have to understand that he does require the time and effort to make sure he progresses and starts to see the world is less scary than he thinks it is.

Gabriel will need more than one meet and greet with his prospective adopters to allow him time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

Gabriel is still waiting for his forever home, I don't know what it's going to take for people to notice this handsome man.

Gabriel recently had a play date with Margate who some of you may have heard of, they went to spend a few hours at a nearby lake with two of our members of staff, and he had a blast. He was on a long line and was free to explore wherever he wanted.

He was so well behaved during the walk, with Margate, the two staff members and when they stopped for ice cream after. He just loves being out adventuring, he wants to sniff everything and explore the world around him, needless to say he was knackered when he returned, had his dinner and went to bed, the sign of a good day.

Gabriel loved his time and the lake, so much so that I'm planning on taking him for another adventure soon that he will hopefully love just as much.

Today I got to spend more time with Gabriel than I usually would so I took advantage of that and we went for a much longer walk.... As usual he was brilliant, he listens, if we need to move out of the way for a car he'll listen to me and move off the road to the side, if he's walking slightly ahead and I call him he stops and turns back.

We also sat around the other side of the rescue where it's usually busier as I want to get him used to being in busier areas and being around people he doesn't know, as he can be a bit reactive.... He did so well, it was fairly busy so he was a little unsure at first but the longer we stayed the better he was, he was good with others around him too, he has come such a long way, but this is something I'm going to keep on working on with him for the foreseeable as we don't know what life he'll have outside of here and he may need to used to busier areas.

We also played with a puzzle feeder today, which he decided would be fun to pick up with his mouth and drop it on the floor to get the treats out faster, he really is a funny boy, but he's super smart too and is quick to pick up tricks especially when there's treats involved.

He really is every Bocker lovers dream and he always gets so overlooked.

He is muzzle trained, and would need to wear his muzzle when meeting new people, dogs or at the vets, but he's also just a big softy who gives the loveliest cwtches and kisses, to be a part of his gang is such an amazing feeling and he shows his affection for you so clearly when he loves you.

This week we’ve had a heatwave which has meant alot of our rescue dogs have needed their ears checked incase they’ve had any mucky build up - Gabriel was one of the unlucky few that have needed some TLC in this area!!We’ve recently had a new meds person who has been visiting Gabriel to do his ear cleans & he has been an absolute angel.
