name: Rachel
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I have never been on walks, but may be too scared and will need some time.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I have had a pea size cyst removed from my right shoulder at the time of spay.

Rachel is a very scared girl who has come to us from a breeder. When she first arrived she was extremely overwhelmed by her new surroundings and clearly hadn’t had much socialisation or handling before. Since being with us, she has slowly started to show small signs of progress as she begins to realise she is safe. Although she still finds being handled very frightening, her kennel mum can now stroke her gently when she's in her bed at the back of the kennel.

She will need a calm and quiet adult-only homewith adopters experienced with traumatised ex-breeding dogs who can provide the reassurance and stability she needs to continue building her confidence and learning about trust and kindness. Her adopters will need to allow her to settle in at her own pace and let her set the speed of her progress as she can still become easily overwhelmed.

Rachel relies on other dogs for comfort and reassurance and will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home who can take her under their wing and help her settle into her new home. They will need to be happy to snuggle up with her and to let her rely on them for support. For some reason she is especially fond of Dachshunds, but she does love all dogs. When she forms a bond with another dog, she absolutely dotes on them and becomes the most loyal best friend to them. It’s so sweet to see.

Day to day, she is a super happy and laid back girl. She LOVES toys and spends a lot of her time chewing on a bone or playing with a plush teddy in one of her beds. She also really loves her food and this has been a great help in gaining her trust and forming a bond with her.

Rachel has never lived in a home before, so she will need very patient and understanding adopters while she settles in and learns all about home life and new skills like house training.She follows a daily routine beautifully, happily running out to the exercise yards and returning to her kennel when it is time to come back in. She is not currently 100% kennel clean, but she is likely to take to toilet training well in a home, as she toilets almost immediately when she goes out into the yard. Her adopters will need to give her plenty of opportunities to go outside while she learns the new routine. Rachel doesn't walk on a lead or harness just yet, but hopefully in the future this is something that we can introduce to her.

The big wide world still feels quite scary for Rachel, but she is beginning to show curiosity in safe environments, and gentle time in the garden will be a great way to help her slowly explore and build confidence. She is not yet cat tested, but we feel cats are unlikely to be an issue for her, although this would need to be assessed appropriately.

Although Rachel has been making progress and will now allow her kennel mum to gently stroke her when she's in a bed in the back of her kennel, she still doesn't enjoy this. She finds being picked up extremely frightening and will panic and does have the potential to bite purely out of fear, so it is imperative that her adopters fully understand her behaviour and are confident managing her needs. We really don’t think she’ll be this way forever, and she’ll get better and better as time goes on, but it would be a lot easier if she was in a home with someone who knew how to help her.

Recently, Rachel needed to have her thick coat clipped during the warm weather, which unfortunately had to be done under sedation as she is not yet ready to be groomed. Despite how frightening this experience must have been for her, she coped far better than we ever expected, allowing herself to be carried to the vets and held for her injection once she was safely in our arms. We couldn't have been prouder of how brave she was. As her coat grows back, we will continue gently introducing her to grooming so she can slowly learn that being brushed doesn't have to be scary.

Rachel has so much potential and, with time, patience and kindness, we truly believe she will continue to make progress and learn that she is safe and loved. She really is an easy dog to care for in every other aspect – she is wonderful with other dogs, thrives on routine and never puts a paw wrong. She just needs a truly understanding home where she can continue building on the trust she has started to develop and finally blossom into the dog she is meant to be.

Rachel came to us with a pea-sized cyst on her shoulder, which was removed at the time of her spay.

Rachel has been given the Gift of Life by Tracy Davidson

Rachel is doing so much better than we expected and is already showing us little glimpses of the lovely girl she could become. She quickly discovered the dog sofas and has found her favourite spot, where she is happiest relaxing alongside her support Dachshund.

Rachel really loves the Dachshunds in the home and will need to be rehomed with at least one calm, friendly and tolerant Dachshund who she can rely on. She is very attached to them and will look for her friend if they are out of sight. She will even approach her fosterer if her Dachshund is sitting on their knee!

Rachel is becoming more inquisitive and has started to approach for a little nose bump on a finger. She will sometimes allow a hand to be offered to her while she is on the sofa and will give a little finger bump in return. She is still not comfortable with being stroked and made it clear that having her face touched was too much for her, so this is something that will need to be respected and worked on slowly.

Rachel is very observant of the other dogs and watches their interactions with people closely. She is still a very scared girl, but she has already exceeded expectations and is beginning to blossom in her foster home. She is happy to share her space with people as long as they do not get too close, and she is even starting to follow basic instructions such as going inside and moving between rooms.

Rachel is settled downstairs in an open crate in the kitchen alongside two Dachshunds and is happy to settle without making any noise. She can be a little destructive with the mats when left for short periods, but overall she is making wonderful progress. We are so pleased to see her beginning to feel safer and more curious about the world around her.

Rachel (or Rachy as I call her) has had quite a few updates on her page now, so I thought I’d do something a little different with this one and basically summarise her and the type of home she needs!

Rachy is a super happy and laid back girl day to day. She LOVES toys and spends a lot of her time chewing on a bone or playing with a plush teddy in one of her beds. She also loves other dogs - especially Dachshunds!! We have no idea why, but she lights up when she’s around them. When she forms a bond with another dog, she absolutely dotes on them and becomes the most loyal best friend to them. It’s so sweet to see. She also loves her food (probably more than anything), and this has been a massive help in gaining her trust and forming a bond with her. She runs to the play yard from her kennel, and back in with no problems, and she also toilets as soon as she gets to the yard every time, so I have a feeling it won’t take long to house train her at all.

Rachy is very easy to look after at the rescue and follows routine beautifully. If you didn’t know anything about her, she looks like quite a normal and happy dog most of the time. But, and this is a big but, she still absolutely hates being touched, and hates being picked up or handled even more. I’ve taken things very slow with her as she isn’t the type of dog you can rush, so I’ve managed to get to the point with her where I can give her gentle strokes when she’s in one of her beds in the back of the kennel. She doesn’t enjoy it, but she does tolerate it now. Picking her up, on the other hand, is a different story. She’s still not used to it and she will still bite to protect herself, so I do have to use a thick blanket to avoid that. I really don’t think she’ll be this way forever, and I do think she’ll get better and better as time goes on, but it would be a lot easier if she was in a home with someone who knew how to help her.

Things such as walking on a lead, grooming, vet visits etc. won’t come easy, but I do believe she will get there and allow these things in the future. She really just needs someone who will love her for who she is, accept her worries and fears, and work with her on them. Most importantly, she needs someone who will never give up on her no matter what.

Rachel’s progress continues slowly and steadily and even though she still doesn’t like to be touched, she is so much more content and calm in general. She’s now more than happy to hang out with me and lay down near me, and just this week she actually went to sleep next to me with her tummy exposed!!! I know that may not sound like a lot, but it’s HUGE for a dog like Rachel with such severe trust issues.

The past couple of weeks at the rescue have been extremely warm and Rachel started to struggle a little bit with having such thick fur, so I decided to get it shaved off. Rachel is still not ready to be groomed, so I did have to take her into the vets to be sedated. This is the first time I’ve had to actually pick her up since I started going the crate and touch work with her, but it had to be done. She does still try her very best to get away and she does still try to bite, but it is less severe than what it was when she first came in. Getting her into my arms was the most difficult part, but after I had hold of her I was able to walk over to the vets carrying her, and hold her while she had her injection without a fuss. I was so, so proud of her. She’s now a bit bald, but so much more comfortable and cooler. When her fur starts to grow back I am going to start introducing her to a brush so she can get used to it, as her coat does grow quite fast and it’s very dense which means it gets matted easily. It’s not ideal for a dog like Rachel needing to be groomed regularly, but I’ll try my very best to ease her into it.

Looking after Rachel on a daily basis is very easy. She follows routine beautifully - running to the play yards and back into her kennel when it’s time to come in. She tries her best to be clean with her toileting and I think if she had access to a garden regularly, she would pick it up really quickly. She also shares everything with her kennel friends perfectly and she never puts a paw wrong with other dogs. Aside from hating being touched, she really isn’t a problem at all. I really am hoping that she’ll start to get used to it soon, and I think she will … but being in a home would help massively. So I hope she doesn’t have to wait too much longer for that to happen.

For the past month, Rachel has officially been my “project dog”. This means I’ve been spending a lot more time working directly with her, and I set a goal for both of us when I started. Because Rachel’s biggest fear is human hands, that became my main focus — helping her feel more comfortable with being touched and gently stroked.

In the first week, I wanted to get her used to my touch without her panicking. When Rachel thinks she’s about to be handled, she’ll run around the kennel, jumping from bed to bed to avoid me, and will bite to protect herself if I get too close. I felt that all the running and panic was only reinforcing her fear, making things harder for both of us. So, I introduced a crate to safely contain her in a smaller space, allowing me to begin gentle handling in a more controlled way.

My hope was that she would start to realise that a soft fuss on her head or body isn’t actually that scary — that the anticipation was worse than the reality. Each day for that first week, I set up a crate at the back of her kennel and spent a short session gently touching her, just once a day to ease her into it.

On the first day, it took a little while for her to go into the crate, but she eventually went in with her friend. She was actually very good and allowed me to gently stroke her face for a few minutes, before becoming a little unsettled and starting to nibble my hand. By the second day, she went into the crate much more quickly and again allowed strokes around her head and under her ears. As I carefully moved further down her body, she became uncomfortable and nibbled a bit harder to let me know she’d had enough.

By the third day, she went straight into the crate, and I focused more on her body. She allowed longer strokes before becoming unsettled. The fourth day was very similar, but on the fifth day there was a real breakthrough — she let me stroke her tummy and chest without any nibbles at all.

After every session, I made sure to sit at the front of her kennel for a few minutes and give her treats so we always ended on a positive note (and to make sure she was still my friend!). Rachel is known to hold a grudge, so maintaining that trust was really important, and thankfully this work hasn’t damaged our relationship at all.

In week two, my goal was to remove the crate and see if she would choose to stay settled in a bed while I handled her. I wasn’t sure how it would go, but she absolutely amazed me. On the first day, she settled into a bed at the back of the kennel while I sat on the floor and gently shuffled towards her — and she stayed still, allowing me to stroke her. I kept things consistent over the next few days without pushing her too far.

By the fifth day, I introduced something new: scissors around her head. She needs a fringe trim, so I wanted to begin desensitising her to the sensation and presence of them. She did incredibly well — so well, in fact, that I managed to snip a tiny bit, which I hadn’t even planned to do. Because she was coping so calmly, I took the opportunity, and it paid off.

In week three, I continued trimming her fringe gradually, little by little. After a few days, I was able to clear the hair from around her eyes.

That’s where we are now. There’s still a long way to go, and Rachel will need plenty more time, patience and love, but I’m so pleased with how far she’s come. We’ve definitely made real progress, and I’m excited to keep building on it with her.

Rachel has been at the rescue for just over a month now and in that time she’s gained a lot of inner confidence, and has blossomed into a very cheeky and happy girl who always seems to be up to mischief!! She absolutely loves toys and gets very excited when I put them in her kennel every morning, and she also loves playing with them in the yards. She’s also very partial to starting ‘parties’ AKA getting all the dogs to have a massive game of chase with her, which she finds very amusing. Her favourite thing in the world though … food!!! She is one of the foodiest dogs I’ve ever met and is always at the front of the queue for breakfast, dinner, and treats.Even though Rachel has made progress in many areas, one thing she still simply can’t handle is being touched by us humans in any way. Her fear of our hands is so strong and she will try to bite to protect herself. This doesn’t mean she’s a nasty dog in any way, it’s just complete panic and fear. It’s something I’m trying to de-sensitise her to and I’m working with her as much as I can, but I do think it’s going to take a long time and a lot of consistency. We don’t know what she’s been through in her life that’s made her the way she is, so all we can do now is prove to her that humans can be kind, and hope that one day she’s able to put her past behind her.Rachel will need a very experienced home with people who will be extremely patient with her, understand her, and work with her through her worries and fears. She’ll need at least 1 resident dog to learn from, and absolutely no children. Things that are normal to most dogs such as going for a walk, being brushed/groomed, or even just having a little fuss, are alien to Rachel, so it’s important her adopters take all of this into consideration and be okay with it.

It may be a long and slow road to get Rachel to where she needs to be, but I promise it will be so worth it. There is no better feeling than a dog like her showing you love and trust for the first time!

Rachel is a very scared girl who has come to us from a breeder. She is a very scared girl at the moment who is quite overwhelmed to find herself here and clearly hasn't had much socialisation before. She is looking for a home with adopters with experience of scared ex-breeding dogs who can provide the reassurance and stability she needs to help build her confidence as she learns about safety, trust, and our intentions.

She will need an adult-only home that can offer a calm and predictable environment where she can take things at her own pace. Rachel will also need at least one kind and confident resident dog to help her settle in and take her under their wing, as she can be easily overwhelmed at the moment.

Rachel has never lived in a home before, so she will need patient and understanding adopters while she learns about house training and how to walk on a lead. Right now, the big wide world may feel too overwhelming for her, so gentle sniffs in the garden would be a good place to start.

Rachel is only acting out of fear, and we have not yet been able to see the girl she will become once she feels safe. She deserves so much love, she just isn’t sure how to accept it yet and will need a truly understanding home to help her blossom.

Rachel has come to us with a pea sized cyst on her shoulder that has been removed at the time of her spay.

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Max
description:
I need an active, breed experienced home that loves playtime!

I’m active and would love a large, secure garden to let off steam.

I walk on the lead but I can pull when excited.

I am house trained but I need to learn some manners.

I have been neutered and am ready for my forever home!

Max is a superstar Lurcher who has been returned to us from his adoptive family. They made the heartbreaking decision to bring him back as he was becoming dominant over the other dog in the home.

He is a very excitable, happy boy - essentially an overgrown puppy in a big body. Max is full of fun and enthusiasm and will need an active home that can meet his exercise and stimulation needs. He already knows some basic commands such as “sit”, “paw”, “lay down”, and “wait”, and he is eager to interact with his people. He is very food oriented, which makes training enjoyable and rewarding, and he already shows lovely food manners, waiting patiently when asked.

Max absolutely loves other dogs and gets incredibly excited when he sees a potential new friend. However, he is still young, full of energy, and not always aware of his size and strength. This can sometimes lead to him becoming overexcited, a little mouthy, and unintentionally overwhelming other dogs. He has been working hard on his social skills and has been socialising while wearing a muzzle for safe and positive interactions. This is purely as a precaution, and his future adopters will need to continue this training and take a responsible approach when introducing him to other dogs.

As he was too much for a more timid dog in his previous home, we feel that Max would be best suited to being homed as an only dog, provided he has plenty of appropriate socialisation with dogs of a similar size and play style. He cannot live with cats or small furries.

As Max has previously lived in a home, he is familiar with household sights and sounds and is house trained. However, he is still working on his lead manners and can pull when he gets excited. Ongoing training, structure, and consistency will be important, along with plenty of mental stimulation to keep his busy mind engaged. He would thrive in a home that can offer activities such as training games or even dog sports.

Max could share his home with older, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 and over, who understand that he can be a bit of a bull in a china shop. Any young people in the home will need to be confident and not worried by an enthusiastic dog who may jump up while he continues to work on his manners.

Max does struggle with separation anxiety and can become destructive if left alone for long periods, so he will need a home where someone is around most of the time and who is committed to helping him gradually build confidence with being left.

Max's new home will need a large, secure garden with 6ft boundaries, where he can let off some steam.

Max will make an amazing addition to a home with experience of similar breeds. He truly is a lovely boy, bouncy, affectionate, and full of life, with so much potential. He is a big-hearted lad who gives his whole heart, and with the right guidance, he will grow into an incredible companion.

Max has recently been castrated, and while he was feeling (understandably) sorry for himself for a few days after, he was brilliant going into the vets and during his recovery. Although he has had to wear a buster collar just to stop him licking at the area, he doesn't let that bother him and is such a good boy when you take it off to take him out for a walk and pop it back on when he's back in his kennel and he has been so easy to give his pain relief medication to as well, he really has been a model patient. He is such an easy dog to handle, given his size he is no issue at all.

During his recovery period, Max has only been on short walks so that he doesn't overdo it in the play yards, but slowly this past week he has been spending some time in our agility yard to have a run and you can definitely see that he is back to his full, playful self, running around, chasing a tennis ball and being inquisitive about anything and everything.

Max is a fantastic boy, and any time I spend with him is just so enjoyable and full of love and fun, he is such a special dog, I'm constantly scratching my head wondering why and how he's still here.

Where do I start with the wonderful ball of energy that is Max.

First and foremost, the question I ask myself and almost everyone that meets Max asks too, how on earth is he still waiting?! A young, handsome, intelligent dog who is BARRELS of fun. There’s something about Max that is just so loveable and he truly does capture people’s hearts. Many of the volunteers who walk him are always so happy to see him and enjoy their time together.

Recently we’ve been working on nailing a ‘touch’ command. When Max is focused he is such a rewarding dog to train. Sometimes his desire to please takes over and he waves his paw at me until I have to accept it (and of course reward because he's the goodest boy no matter what). He is also learning to be calmer when greeting people and has even had some gentle fuss from some children too. It remains true that Max cannot be homed with children under the age of 16, but it is so important for Max to have positive interactions with respectful children to prevent any reactivity / fear from developing. It also helps teach him to be calm when meeting new people, especially when they’re smaller than him!

Max brings such a unique type of energy to the rescue, he is such a joyful boy and truly comes alive when he is with his people. I threw Max a 1st birthday party and all of his favourite people came throughout the day to play with him and bring him yummy treats, fuss and cuddles. He had the best day and it was so touching to see how loved he is despite not being in a home.

We are doing our very best to raise Max into a well rounded, well socialised and well adjusted adult dog. However, he is at such a crucial stage in his development and has already spent 5 months in kennels. It’s no place for a young dog to grow up. Nearly half of his life spent in kennels patiently waiting for his second chance to come and take him home.

Despite his size Max really is just a baby and definitely a lap dog too. So if you have a spot on the sofa you can share, Max will happily join you and be the bestest friend anyone could wish for.

Myself and Max have formed a very close bond over the last few months we’ve been working together. We take daily walks, go to the big play yard and have plenty of cuddles and fusses.I’m not sure what it is about Max that keeps getting him overlooked, it could be his size or that he is like a big playful puppy or something else, whatever it is, anyone would be lucky to have this handsome chap in their lives, he will always put a smile on your face and he has such a good sense of humour, watching him having zoomies in his kennel yard while he’s jumping off the obstacles in there then stoping then going back round again is nothing short of entertaining, or when he’s fishing treats out of the paddling pool while simultaneously blowing bubbles with his nose.Max truly deserves the world, he is such a sweet and caring boy with a big personality and so much love to give, as well as his big size there is also a big heart and all he wants is to be able to fully give it to someone and finally find his forever home.

Max is a big, happy baby with bags of energy and so much love to give. He is an excitable, affectionate boy who adores attention and loves having people around him. He is always happy to greet you and be part of whatever is going on.

As Max is still young and growing, he is slowly learning his manners and how to greet people politely without jumping. . He will need adopters who can match his energy, continue his training, and give him the stimulation, guidance, and love he needs to thrive.

Max is a gentle, overlooked soul who is learning new things every day at the rescue, but he is missing the comforts of home. He cannot wait to find a family who understands him and can help him blossom into the wonderful companion he is meant to be.With the right home, patience, and plenty of love, Max will make a loyal and joyful best friend.

Since coming back into our care, Max has been working hard on learning how to socialise with other dogs. He absolutely adores them and gets incredibly excited when he sees a potential new friend! Because he’s still young, full of beans, and a bit unaware of his own size, he can sometimes be a little too enthusiastic. This can lead to him becoming overexcited, a bit mouthy, and unintentionally overwhelming other dogs.

To help him learn safe and positive interactions, Max has been socialising while wearing a muzzle. This is purely for his safety and that of other dogs, and his future adopters will need to continue this training and take a responsible approach when introducing him to new canine companions. Aside from that, Max is everything you’d want in a young pup he's bouncy, happy, affectionate, and full of life.

He’s very food oriented, which makes training a dream! He already knows commands like “sit” and has learned great food manners where be waits patiently until he’s told he can eat. Max thrives on mental stimulation and ongoing training, and with the right guidance, he has all the potential to grow into an incredible dog. Max does struggle with separation anxiety and can become destructive if left alone for long periods. He really craves human company so he’ll need a home where someone is around most of the time and is committed to helping him build confidence being alone gradually. He’s such a loving, handsome boy who gives his whole heart, and it would be wonderful to see him back in a home environment where he can truly thrive. As a young pup, he’s missed out on some important early experiences, so a patient, committed family will make all the difference in helping him become the best version of himself.

He is a very excitable, happy boy - essentially an overgrown puppy in a big body. Max is full of fun and enthusiasm and will need an active home that can meet his exercise and stimulation needs. He already knows some basic commands such as “sit”, “paw”, “lay down”, and “wait”, and he is eager to interact with his people.

Max loves other dogs but is often unaware of his size and strength, having grown into such a big lad very quickly. As he is still just a puppy, he is still learning about manners and can be mouthy and plays in a very typical Lurcher way. In his previous home, there was an incident when he was around 3 months old, where he was a little too rough and resulted in a small dog needing veterinary treatment. He has started muzzle training for off-lead play as a precaution, and he will need a home that understands Lurcher play styles and is confident managing this appropriately. We have been socialising him with dogs of all sizes on walks and he is doing very well.

As Max has previously lived in a home, he is familiar with household sights and sounds and is house trained. However, he is still working on his lead manners and can pull when he gets excited. Ongoing training and consistency will be important.

Max will make an amazing addition to a home with experience of similar breeds. He truly is a lovely boy. He is a big-hearted, affectionate lad who is still convinced he can curl up and fit on your lap.

name: Rhea
description:
I could live with dog-savvy teens who respect my space.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I have bilateral cataracts & I will be spayed before adoption!

08-11-26 Rhea has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. She is a worried little girl who is a little overwhelmed to find herself here at the moment. She can be quite timid when she first meets you, but after a while she does start to come out of her shell and will accept a fuss with a little waggy tail. She is also starting to become quite nosey and inquisitive, which is lovely to see.

Rhea will be looking for a loving home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and will allow her to settle in at her own pace. She currently relies on her kennel friends for comfort and reassurance, so she will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home who she can look to as she begins to find her feet. Rhea does show some signs of resource guarding around food and can grumble at other dogs, so she will need to be fed separately from any other dogs in her new home. This is specifically around sharing food with other dogs, rather than with people. Her adopters will need to be confident in managing this and helping her feel comfortable at mealtimes.

Rhea has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to be patient and understanding as she learns about the routines of home life, including house training and walking on a lead. Having a confident canine companion to show her the ropes will be a big help as she builds her confidence and starts to discover the world outside the rescue.

Rhea could share her home with dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 and over, who can appreciate and understand that she will need a gentle, quiet introduction to the home and her own space to settle in.

Rhea is a sweet, timid girl who will need a little extra time, kindness and reassurance to help her find her paws. With the right home and a lovely doggy friend by her side, we hope she will gradually grow in confidence and learn to enjoy all the comforts of home life.

Rhea has arrived with bilateral cataracts, which does not seem to be bothering her at this time but will need to be monitored in her future home.

Rhea has been given the Gift of Life by Rosalind Steven

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. name: Dutch
description:
I could live with dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who respect my space.

I need to be the only dog in my new home. No cats please!

I walk well on a lead and muzzle trained. I would enjoy an active lifestyle!

Please be patient with me, I haven’t lived in a home before.

I am already vaccinated and neutered and ready for my new home!

Dutch is an incredible boy who has come into our care from a pound in Ireland in search of a fresh start. Unfortunately, we don't know much about his history, but what we do know is that he is one of the most loving and affectionate dogs you could ever hope to meet, with a heart as big as his personality. Dutch simply wants to be close to his people, whether that's following you around, leaning into you for fuss, or curling up beside you for cuddles. Being with the people he loves is all he really wants.

Dutch would love to find a home with adopters who are around for most of the day and can include him in everyday life. He thrives on human companionship and will make a wonderfully devoted shadow to his new family. He will need adopters who have experience with similar breeds and understand typical breed traits, including prey drive and the need for appropriate mental and physical enrichment.

Dutch would be best suited to life as an only dog. Although he can socialise well with other dogs of a similar size, he can become overexcited and mouthy, which may lead to frustration. Because of this, he is muzzle trained and wears a muzzle during social interactions to help him continue building positive experiences. He cannot live with cats or small furries.

As Dutch has never lived in a home before, he will need support with house training and learning the general routines of family life. He is such a clever boy and always tries his very best to do the right thing, so we are confident he will enjoy learning with patient, positive guidance.

Dutch already walks well on a lead, although he can occasionally be reactive when passing other kennels. This is understandable in a busy rescue environment and may be something his adopters will need to continue working on. He is an energetic, happy-go-lucky boy who is more than ready to start exploring the world with his new family. An active home where he can enjoy plenty of walks, enrichment, training and quality time with his people would suit him perfectly.

Dutch could share his home with older, dog-savvy teenagers who can appreciate that he will need a gentle introduction to his new surroundings and his own space to settle in.

Dutch is bright, affectionate and full of love. He has so much to offer and is simply looking for someone to love as much as he loves them. For the right family, he will be an incredibly loyal, fun-loving and devoted companion.

Dutch has a passport and travel document.

Dutch has been given the Gift of Life by Louise Southward

I’m truly so sad that Dutch is still waiting for his forever home. It’s such a shame that certain breeds can be so easily overlooked.

Dutch is the most sweet, loving, loyal and clever boy. He absolutely loves everyone, has bags of confidence and is always bursting with excitement to say hello to everyone he meets out on a walk.

We've recently started walking Dutch with different friends each day to help him learn to manage some of his reactivity, and honestly, after just one walk, the very next day he was absolutely brilliant!

Dutch isn't reactive because he wants to be difficult, he's simply so excited and eager to say hello that he's still learning how to manage those feelings.

He's such a smart boy and has picked things up so quickly. He just needs someone who will keep that clever brain busy, give him some guidance and help him continue to learn.

Please don't overlook Dutch. There is so much to love about this boy, and we would love nothing more than to see him finally find his forever home.

I still can’t quite understand how this incredibly smart and loving boy hasn’t found his forever home yet.If you’re looking for a dog to train, learn new tricks and go on lots of adventures with, then Dutch really is your boy.He’s the best of both worlds a crazy, energetic boy who also absolutely loves his people and loves nothing more than a good snuggle.

Dutch, or as I like to call him, Dutchy, is honestly one of the most loving and affectionate boys you could ever hope to meet.

He's the kind of dog who just wants to be close to you. Whether it's following you around, leaning into you for fuss, or curling up for cuddles, being with his people is all he really wants. Watching him have to go back into his kennel after spending time together is heartbreaking because kennel life is just no place for a boy like him.

What makes it even sadder is that he hasn't received a single application. If I'm honest, my biggest worry is that he'll become one of our long-stay dogs, and my heart breaks at the thought of that because he simply doesn't deserve it.

He's such a clever boy and always tries so hard to do the right thing. He recently went on his first long walk with one of our wonderful regular volunteers and was an absolute angel. He took everything in his stride and made everyone so proud.

He's also been having play dates with our lovely girl, Swanny, to help him burn off some of that doggy energy while learning good doggy manners.

At the end of the day, Dutchy is just a baby. He's got the biggest heart, so much love to give, and he deserves a home where he'll be someone's whole world instead of waiting behind kennel doors. I know his family is out there somewhere; I just hope they find him before he spends another day wondering why no one has chosen him.

Dutch is an incredible boy who has come into our care from a pound in Ireland in search of a fresh start. Unfortunately, we don't know much about his history, but what we do know is that he is one of the most loving and affectionate dogs you could ever hope to meet.

He would love to find a loving home with adopters who are around most of the time and would have plenty of time to spend with him. He would need adopters who have experience with similar breeds and experience with his typical breed traits like prey drive etc.

Dutch would be best suited to being homed as an only dog as although he does socialise well with other dogs of his size, he can become over excited and mouthy which can lead to frustration. For this reason he is being trained to wear a muzzle when socialising. He cannot be homed with cats or small furries.

As Dutch has never lived in a home before, he will need to learn all about house training and the other basics of home life. With patience and guidance, we think he will adapt well and enjoy all the comforts a home has to offer.

Dutch can already walk well on a lead, though he can be a little reactive when passing other kennels, this is understandable in a busy rescue environment, but may be something his adopters will need to work with him on. He is an energetic and incredibly lovely bo who ie is happy-go-lucky in nature and is more than ready to start adventuring with his new adopters. He would love an active home where he can enjoy plenty of walks, enrichment, and quality time with his people.

Dutch could share his home with older, dog-savvy teenagers who can appreciate and understand that he will need a gentle and quiet introduction to the home, along with his own space to settle in.

He is a bright, affectionate, and fun-loving boy who is sure to make a wonderful and loyal companion for a lucky family.

Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

name: Archie
description:
I'd like a quiet, adult-only home to help me relax and feel safe.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I walk well on a lead and would enjoy one or two walks a day!

I have lived in a home so I know the basics.

I have been neutered and have had 21 teeth removed.

Archie is such a sweet little man who came into our care from a breeder. He was adopted but has sadly been returned after his adopters felt they were not the right match for him. Archie formed a very strong bond with his female owner, but found it much harder to build a relationship with her husband, who was frequently away from home and therefore had very little opportunity to gain Archie's trust. When Archie becomes closely bonded to his favourite person, he can become protective of them. In his previous home, he nipped when he was sitting with his owner and her husband approached, so his new adopters will need to understand this behaviour and be prepared to continue building his confidence in a positive and patient way.

He is a cuddly and affectionate little dog once he feels comfortable, although he isn't quite brave enough to take treats from our hands just yet. Although Archie gets on well with other dogs, he can become protective of his favourite person around them, so we think he would be happiest as the only dog in the home, where he can relax and build a close bond with his new family.

As Archie has lived in a home before, he will already be familiar with the sights and sounds of home life. However, he may need a little reminding of his house training in a new environment. He walks well on a lead and enjoys his walks with volunteers.

Archie is looking for a quiet, adult-only home with adopters who have experience of the breed and of rescue dogs. He will need people who are happy to give him the time and space he needs to settle and understand that he is safe.

Archie is doing really well since returning to us and his confidence is growing all the time. He is such a loving little dog, and in the right home, we hope he will continue to thrive and become a devoted companion.

We absolutely love this little guy at the rescue, Archie may be small but his personality is mighty. He is funny, lovable and impossible not to love. Archie is still a tiny bit shy with new people but it’s taking him less and less time to open up to new people and dogs. Archie loves to play with tennis balls, smother you with kisses and generally amuse us with his cheeky personality. Archie would like a child-free home as he is still a little anxious at times.

Archie is an absolute pleasure to work with! It’s been some time now, and our bond continues to grow stronger every day.He absolutely loves smothering you with kisses and will do anything to get himself onto your lap! Archie has been kennelled with a few dogs and socialised with plenty more, but he has become particularly taken with a Cocker called Trixie. They share some similar traits, including not wanting to share their humans, although neither has displayed any jealousy towardsthe other so far. They absolutely love running laps around the yard together before heading straight into your lap for some fuss. Archie will even stand on Trixie’s back just to make sure he gets in on the action and doesn’t miss out on any attention!As mentioned, Archie is yet to display any jealous traits towards either dogs or humans, but that doesn’t mean he won’t potentially show this once settled into a home. It’s something any potential adopter should be mindful of and prepared to manage appropriately.

What I can promise, though, is that Archie will become your best friend. He has so much love to give and, once he trusts you, he will love you unconditionally.This gorgeous boy deserves someone who will give him the love, patience and understanding he needs — and in return, you’ll have a loyal companion who will want nothing more than to be by your side.

Archie is the funniest and cheekiest of little Dachshunds. Archie needs a little time to warm to you (but not all that long), and once he does, he is the most lovely of boys. I have been caring for him for a few weeks now, and I am totally smitten.

Archie walks beautifully on lead and loves nothing more than when we venture out for a stroll along the lanes around the rescue. Archie is very fond of his toys and will happily run around the yard with a ball in his mouth. He will also spend much time organising his cuddly toys, making sure they are in just the right place.

Archie has been kennelled with other small female dogs. He seems to do best with robust smaller females, as he can be a little frisky with the more timid dogs. Archie could go as an only dog in the right home, one where there are humans who will have lots of time for him.

Archie is very enthusiastic with his kisses once he knows you and will desperately clamber over you for fusses. Archie is an all-round lovely little dog, best suited to a quiet adult home where there is plenty of love, time, and patience for him to truly settle in.

Archie is a gorgeous little boy who came to us from a breeder and was understandably unsure of the world around him. It was truly heartbreaking to see how frightened he was as he would shy away from human contact and retreat when approached. Archie needs gentle handling, patience, and calm, slow movements to help him feel safe. Already, we are seeing progress. He enjoys a gentle fuss and has grown some confidence wagging his tail enthusiastically.

He gains reassurance from other dogs and will need a kind, confident resident dog in his new home to help guide him, boost his confidence, and show him that people and home life can be safe and rewarding.

Archie has never lived in a home before, so his adopters will need to be patient and understanding as he learns the basics, including house training and walking on a lead. He could share his home with older, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 and over, who can appreciate and understand that he will need a gentle, quiet introduction to the home and his own space to settle in.

Since arriving with us, Archie has undergone extensive and much-needed dental treatment and has had 21 teeth removed. He is now recovering well and feeling much more comfortable.

name: Milo
description:
I will need an adult-only home that understands me.

I will need to be the only dog in my new home, so all of the attention is on me!

I will need an extra secure garden, at least 6ft+ where I will be safe!

I walk well on a lead but will need my adopters to be understanding of my needs!

I have lived in a home before so may I may already know the basics.

I will be neutered before finding my forever home!

06-10-26 Milo is a super sweet boy who has come to us from a home through no fault of his own. Sadly, he has already been through more changes than a young dog should have to, and he is understandably a little worried in new environments. He takes a lot of comfort from people he knows, but once he feels comfortable, his fun and affectionate personality really starts to shine.

Milo is an incredibly sweet boy who absolutely loves being close to his people and thinks he is the perfect lap dog! He is happiest when he can have a cuddle and will happily climb up for a lap sit. He is a sensitive little soul and will need a kind and patient home where he can continue to build his confidence and learn that he is safe and secure.

Milo will be looking for a home where he can be the only dog and get all the fuss and attention for himself. We are told that he has had a previous incident with a cat and so he cannot be homed with cats or small furries and must be kept on lead unless in a secure area.

Milo has missed out on some socialisation, but he is currently working on his social skills and is making lovely progress. He can happily walk alongside calm dogs and has had some nice greetings. He doesn't always know what to make of other dogs yet and can sometimes get a little carried away when mixing, but with continued positive socialisation we are sure his confidence will grow. He can also react if another dog barks at him first while on lead, so his new family will need to understand this and help him learn how to navigate these situations.

Milo will need an adult-only home with people who have experience of bull breeds and understand what sensitive souls they can be.Although he is a wonderful boy, he would not be suitable for a first time dog owner.He will need a kind and patient family who can give him time to settle and continue building his confidence. He will also need the time he is left home alone built up gradually as he settles into his new home.

Milo will need an extra secure garden of at least 6ft to keep him safe, as he is a young and active boy who could be an escape artist if given the opportunity.

Milo is such a lovely young boy who has already been through so much change. With the right family, patience and continued socialisation, we know he will make a wonderful companion and be the loving, fun little lap dog he is so desperate to be.

name: Jinx
description:
I'd like a quiet, adult-only home to help me relax and feel safe.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I will need a secure garden with minimum 6ft fencing.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I have a sore eye that is being monitored.

Jinx is an exceptionally frightened boy who has come into our care from a breeder. He will do all he can to run away and hide from us, and it is heartbreaking to witness just how scared he is. However, after just over a month in our care, his personality is slowly beginning to shine through. Although he remains very wary and unsure, he is starting to make lovely little steps forward. He now gets excited when he sees a familiar face, happily wagging his tail and sniffing a hand, even if he isn't quite ready for anyone to come too close. These may seem like small steps, but for Jinx they are huge achievements, and it is wonderful to see his confidence growing.

Jinx has also begun harness training and is taking to it really well! He is now venturing down to our big play yard, where his playful puppy side is starting to emerge. It is lovely to see him becoming a little more curious about the world around him as he gradually learns that he is safe.

Jinx will need a kind and confident resident dog in his new home, as this will be a much-needed support system to help him settle and gain confidence. We have not yet cat tested him, but given what we have seen so far, we feel it is unlikely that he would be suitable to share a home with cats.

As Jinx has never lived in a home before, he will need to learn all about house training and the other basics of home life. His harness training is progressing well, but his adopters will need to continue this gently and at his own pace. He will need a quiet, experienced home with people who understand ex-breeding dogs and appreciate that building trust with him will take considerable time, patience and kindness.

Due to his nervous nature, Jinx is currently a flight risk and will need a very secure garden with boundaries of at least 6ft. He may also need to be muzzled for formal handling, such as veterinary visits, to help keep everyone safe and make these experiences as comfortable as possible for him.

Jinx arrived with a sore eye, so we are continuing to clean it and make sure he is comfortable while we assess this further.

Jinx still has a long way to go, but he is making progress every day, and it is lovely to see his gentle, playful personality beginning to emerge. He needs a very special home filled with patience and love, where his adopters understand that trust will take time and are happy to celebrate every little achievement along the way. With the support of a kind canine companion and people who will let him move at his own pace, we hope Jinx will continue to blossom and discover the safe and loving life he deserves.

Jinx has been given the Gift of Life by Lesley Beattie

Jinx has now been with us just over a month, and although Jinx is still a very scared boy, his personality is slowly starting to shine through. Jinx has now begun harness training and is taking to it really well! He even now adventures down to our big play yard where his puppy side is really starting to show!  Jinx also now gets really excited to see me, he doesn’t allow me very close but he will happily wag his tail, and sniff my hand!

This might sound like the smallest thing, but for myself and Jinx this is a massive win! Every day is confidence is showing more and more.

Jinx just needs a home with loads of patience and love, and people who will understand trust is going to a long time.I can’t wait to see Jinx blossom more and more each day.

name: Paris
description:
I'd like a quiet, experienced, adult-only home to help me relax and feel safe.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

30-09-26 Paris is a scared girly who is not used to being handled. She has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start and is not a fan of human touch at the moment.

When we have needed to get close to Paris for health checks, we have had to carefully corner her so that we can pick her up. She panics and shakes, but she does allow us to handle her and, once she is safely in our arms, she eventually cuddles into us and allows us to carry out her checks. This shows us that although she is very frightened, she is beginning to understand that we are not going to hurt her.

Paris will need another kind and confident dog in her new home, and this dog will be a much-needed support system for her as she settles in and starts to find her confidence.

As Paris has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training and the other basics of home life. She will need an ex-breeding experienced, adult-only home with adopters who understand just how much patience and reassurance she will need.

Paris is a very worried little girl right now, but once she is given the security of being held, we can see that there is a much softer side to her. We hope that with time, patience and the support of a reassuring canine companion, she will slowly learn to trust and enjoy the happy new start she deserves.

Paris has been given the Gift of Life by Margaret Hunter

name: Irene
description:
I can live with older, dog savvy teenagers, aged 16+ who respect my space.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I am new to lead walking, and would like to continue this once I have settled in.

I have lived in a home before so know the basics.

I have Grade 3 bilateral luxating patellas.

21-10-26 Irene is a nervous little lady who has come to us from a breeder. Although she is still unsure, she shows lovely glimpses of wanting to be confident. If you are patient with her and crouch down to her level, she'll quietly come over to give you little kisses, showing just how much love she has to give once she feels safe.

Irene will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home that she can lean on as she learns about trust and settles into home life. She has recently moved to a foster home where she is learning all about the routines of home life. She can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who are sensible and will allow her time to settle in. She will need a home that has experience with ex-breeders that can provide her with the assurance she deserves.

Irene is new to lead walking but has enjoyed plenty of walks with her foster mummy and is gaining her confidence on the lead. She will need a home without cats as she has met cats while out and about and was a little too interested in them. Irene is a truly lovely girl who just needs time, patience and plenty of TLC. With an understanding home and a canine friend by her side, we're sure she will continue to grow in confidence and become a wonderful companion.

Irene has been assessed by our vets who have noted that she has Grade 3 bilateral luxating patellas. These aren't causing her any issues at the moment and may improve with gentle exercise as she builds muscle. They will need to be monitored by her adopters and their vet and her adopters should be aware that any future treatment relating to her luxating patellas will not be covered by insurance.

Irene has been given the Gift of Life by Trudie Williams

name: Helga
description:
I can live with older children, aged 13+, who understand I need time to settle in.

I would like to be the only animal in my new home.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I walk well on a lead and would enjoy one or two walks a day!

I have lived in a home before so know the basics.

I have been spayed & am ready for my forever home! Read below for more!

25-09-26 Helga is a wonderful lady who originally came to us a while ago and was adopted into a loving home, where she spent several happy years. Sadly, she has now returned to our care as it wasn't the right long-term match for her needs, and she is looking for a new home that understands her and can give her the life she deserves.

Helga generally mixes well with other dogs, but she can be quite selective about who she likes and can be unpredictable around certain dogs. For this reason, she will need to be the only dog in her new home, and her adopters will need previous experience with reactive dogs and an understanding of how to manage her around other dogs when out and about. She cannot live with cats or small furries and will also need to be kept on lead around birds and livestock.

When it comes to people, Helga is a complete big baby! She doesn't quite understand her size (47kg!) and loves nothing more than getting as close to you as possible, and will use your legs as her very own leaning post while she soaks up all the fuss. She has quickly become a favourite with everyone she meets and is such a lovely girl to have around. Despite her size, she has a lovely, calm temperament with people and is incredibly affectionate once she knows you.

She is an outgoing lady that would love to go on plenty of quiet adventures where she can enjoy the outdoors in peace. However, she can also be a lazy lady, and would love a home where she can enjoy being a couch potato.

Helga can live with sensible, dog-savvy older teenagers aged 13+ who understand her needs and will treat her with kindness and respect. Due to her size and strength, she can be quite strong on the lead, so any children in the home should not be responsible for walking her, as she could potentially overpower them if she reacts or becomes excited while out.

Having already lived in a home for several years, Helga understands the basics of home life and is house trained. However, her adopters should be prepared to give her a little patience and some gentle reminders while she settles back into a new routine. Moving home can be a big change, and we want Helga to have the time she needs to feel comfortable and secure again.

Helga is an amazing lady who has so much love to give. She does have some specific needs, but for the right person who understands her and is experienced with reactive dogs, she could be a wonderful companion. She just needs someone willing to look past her quirks, understand what makes her tick and give her the chance to find the right forever home.

Helga has arrived overweight and is now on a diet to help her back to a healthy weight. Her back legs seem to be affected by this and she is now on joint supplements to help her joints as she continues to lose the weight.

Helga's previous adopters had her DNA tested and this came back as 46% Giant Schnauzer, 44% Caucasian Shepherd Dog, 3% Saint Bernard, 2% Black Russian Terrier & 2% German Shepherd Dog.

name: Gigi
description:
I will need an adult-only home that understands me.

I need a resident dog Cocker Spaniel size or larger to be my friend.

I would like a secure garden with 6ft+ fences.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have been spayed & am ready for my forever home!

Gigi is a very worried lady who has come to us from a breeder. When she first arrived, she was terrified of people and would try to escape any area she was in if she thought someone might approach her. Thankfully, she has made lovely progress and is now much more relaxed around the carers she knows. She has settled into her routine and will even come over for little sniffs when her kennel friends approach for attention. She is also much easier to handle now and, when worried, will retreat to her safe corner rather than trying to flee.

Despite her progress, Gigi remains a flight risk and her safety must always be a priority. Her adopters will need to be very safety-conscious and have a very secure garden with fencing at least 6ft high. Moving to a new environment may cause her confidence to regress, so precautions will be essential to keep her safe. We hope to begin harness training with her, but this will need to be introduced slowly and carefully. Double-leading will be absolutely essential for a long time to come.

Gigi absolutely loves other dogs and is delighted to meet them, wanting to be friends with everyone! She will need a kind, confident resident dog who genuinely enjoys canine company and can take her under their wing, helping her feel secure and guiding her through the different aspects of home life. She will need this dog to be Cocker Spaniel sized or larger and cannot be homed with smaller dogs.

As Gigi has never lived in a home before, she will need patient adopters who can help her learn about house training, lead walking and all the new experiences that come with being a much-loved pet. She needs an adult-only home with experience of ex-breeding dogs, where her fears are understood and she is given the time, space and reassurance she needs to settle at her own pace.

Gigi has come a long way already, and with the right home, a loving canine companion and plenty of time and patience, we believe she has the potential to continue blossoming. Her new family must be prepared to put in as much time and effort as she needs, taking everything slowly and steadily so she can learn that life can be a wonderful place to be.

Gigi has been given the Gift of Life by Rachel Morris

When Gigi was first moved in to her current section she was terrified, she would try to jump out of any area she was in if she felt a human may be getting near to her, now she has settled into the routine and knows the carers of the section well, she is far more relaxed with them, even coming up for little sniffs when her kennel friends do. She is much easier to handle now too and will freeze in her safe corner in her kennel rather than trying to flee.

Despite the progress she has made her new adopters will be very safety conscious with a very secure garden to ensure that if she were to regress when brought in to a new environment she would always still be safe. We feel that with the progress she has made we can now start to harness train her, this will be a slow process always keeping her safety at the forefront of our minds and double leading her will be absolutely essential for a long time to come.

Gigi loves other dogs, any dog she meets makes her very happy and she truly wants to be a friend to them all, so she will need a resident dog who actively loves having a companion and will really take her under their wing and help to guide her through all aspects of home life.

In the right home she will thrive but her new humans will need to be prepared to put in as much time, effort and patience as she needs and to take it slow and steady so she truly learns to see that life is actually pretty good after all.

Gigi is a very worried lady who has come to us from a breeder and is understandably very nervous and uncomfortable around people. She can be considered a flight risk as she will do her best to get away when she feels worried, so she will need very slow and gentle introductions to the world around her.

Gigi is going to need lots of TLC, patience and understanding from her new family as she learns that she is safe and begins to build her confidence. She will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home who she can look to and lean on for reassurance as she settles in.

Gigi has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to be patient and understanding as she learns about house training and walking on a lead. These things may take some time, and she will need a family who is happy to let her progress at her own pace. She will need a very secure garden with fences 6ft+.

Gigi will need an adult-only home with ex-breeding experience, where her needs can be understood and she can receive the patience and reassurance she deserves. With time, love and the support of a confident canine companion, we hope Gigi will slowly learn to trust and become the happy, active girl we know she can be.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Vera
description:
Gorgeous Vera is a 3-year-old, fun-loving young Lurcher with lots of enthusiasm for life. Vera will need to be the only pet in her new home, although she enjoys spending time with other dogs and would benefit from having regular walking friends to help develop her social skills. She could live with older secondary school-aged children who are confident around large, boisterous breeds. Like a typical young Lurcher, Vera is springy on her long legs and can be excitable when out and about. She can jump up when greeting people and can be boisterous when walking on a lead, so she'll need patient and confident adopters who are committed to continuing her loose lead walking training. Vera will need her leaving hours built up gradually from very short periods once she has settled into her new home. She can also find travelling in the car difficult, so her adopters will need to help her with a safe way to travel and create positive experiences around car journeys.
Vera would benefit from a home that can offer her plenty of exercise, company and opportunities to explore.

Vera is a curious girl with a real spring in her step when she knows it’s time for a walk! She loves getting out and about, is always keen to see what’s around the next corner and never turns down some attention from her favourite people. One of Vera's most endearing qualities is her playful and joyful nature. She's always ready for an adventure and loves getting involved in family life. While she's still learning her manners and social skills, she's a bright young dog with lots of potential. She’s friendly, affectionate and wonderfully easy to like, making her the sort of girl who could quickly become the best companion.

If you're looking for an active companion and are prepared to help a lively young Lurcher continue her training and confidence-building, Vera could be the perfect addition to your family. Be sure to add her to your favourites and submit an apply to adopt application.

name: Mitzi
description:
Meet Mitzi our 11yr old Mini Daxi. He is a sensitive chap so is looking for an adult only home that have plenty of time to build a relationship with him and help guide him in areas that cause him worry. Mitzi has previously lived with cats and can do so again in his next home following gradual introductions.

Mitzi has struggled with his change in environment and needs extra support settling into his new home. He is looking for a home where someone is around majority of time with a view of this being built up gradually, as well as reintroducing housetraining and building his confidence with car travel. Mitzi walks beautifully on lead and enjoys his meal times. He will thrive in a quieter home environment.

name: Aria
description:
Aria is a 7 month old Pointer X Spaniel. She is a friendly girl who could join a home with children of Primary School age and older who are confident around bouncy dogs as she may jump up when excited. Aria has been able to mix both on and off lead with other dogs and has the potential to live with another dog pending meets at the centre. She would benefit from a garden to provide space for play and housetraining however this is not essential if ample alternative outlets for exercise are provided. Once settled, leaving hours could be built up.

Aria is a sweet, young girl looking for an active family that can help teach her the basics and give her the time and exercise she needs. She will make a wonderful companion for her new family.

name: Milo
description:
Milo is a 3-year-old Terrier Crossbreed looking for a family who will have low leaving hours, as Milo struggles to be left on his own. He would love a family where someone would be able to be home with him for the majority of the day and work on building up his alone time. Milo could live with younger secondary-aged children and have visitors in the home who are older primary-school-aged and older, as long as they respect his space and leave him be when resting. Milo has the potential to live with a well-matched dog, pending meets at the centre.

Milo is the cutest bean who adores going out on new adventures with his owners, followed by cuddles with the family back at home for a well-earned nap. He is a sweet, playful boy who loves having company and throwing his toys around. This cheeky boy is very smart (and food-motivated), so he would do great learning new skills. Could he be your pawfect match?

name: Crystal
description:
Crystal is looking for a home that will be able to fulfil her desire to explore and have energy levels to match hers! She has shown us that she can settle when things are calm, but her personality shines through when she can be out and about exploring, sniffing or playing!

Crystal can live with a family with secondary school aged children and above. She’s a friendly, playful dog who likes to spend time with people, so would love a family that are around during the day. She doesn’t require a garden as long as her adopters are happy to take her to secure fields for off-lead exercise. Although she cannot live with dogs, she has got the potential to work on her socialisation with other dogs on walks.

name: Bonnie
description:
Meet Bonnie, a beautiful 2yr Lurcher Crossbreed. She is a super friendly, affectionate young dog who will make a fantastic pet for the right home. This clever girl loves playing on agility equipment and has so much PAW-tential! She’d love adopters who’d enjoy lots of activities and adventures with her. Bonnie has a lot going for her, she is great at travelling in cars, is house-trained and walks nicely on a lead (she can be a bit pully at times, but this is very manageable!)

Bonnie is sweet-natured, energetic and at times quite bouncy! Because of this she could be wonderful for a family but may be too much for younger Primary school children. Bonnie is very tolerant of other dogs and may be able to live with another one depending on a successful dog mix. She would also happily live as the only dog in her new home. 
Bonnie could be perfect for you if you’re looking for an active, friendly dog to have loads of fun with through training, adventures and snuggles!

name: Darcie
description: Meet the gorgeous pair Darcie and Gracie! Darcie is a loving, affectionate girl with SO much love to give. Darcie and Gracie have always been together and enjoy spending time with one another, so will be looking for a family happy to take on a pair! Darcie enjoys spending her day sunbathing out in the garden, followed by a snooze in her bed. Darcie loves playing with Gracie, they both love a tennis ball and will happily share toys! Darcie loves exploring on her walks and will happily say hello to people and other dogs! Darcie needs support getting in and out the car, but she is great in the car travelling. Darcie would be best suited to a home with upper primary school children and above. Could you offer this lovely pair their forever home? AWE licence number 13090 by West Lothian Council.

name: Willow
description:
Willow is very sweet affectionate and clever girl looking for outdoor adventures with her new family.  She is looking for a adult only home that is calm and quiet, with a consistent daily routine. Willow will need a home with a private garden to chill out in and an area indoors suitable for baby gates to be put into place, which will help with her routine around spaces and visitors. Potential adopters will need to be able to commit to multiple meets at the centre to get to know her at her pace.  She loves her treats, and this will be great motivator for her continued training  when in the home environment.

Willow is a sweet affectionate girl who loves a fuss and chilling out on the sofa with her favourite people. She loves running around and playing with her toys and is learning to search for them when they are hidden around the garden. Willow loves nothing more than long sniffy walks, paddling in the river and meeting up with her dog friends for a walk. Even though she does socialise with other dogs, Willow would prefer to be the only pet in the home. Willow has learnt to be protective about her space, so advice will be given on how to manage this in the home on a daily basis and when visitors should visit.  It would help Willow if she had her own 'safe' space to go to if she feels unsure around unknown people coming into the home or if she just needs time-out to herself.  
Once you are besties with Willow, she is the most affectionate and loyal dog to go on adventures with! She is good in the car and will sit nicely on the back seat with a harness safely attached. She is a very intelligent dog and loves to learn new tricks and commands and this is a good way to build that bond with her.  If you think you can offer Willow a home and are willing to continue on with her training needs, then with time and patience, she has the potential to flourish in the home.

name: Pooky
description:
Pooky is a striking 2.5-year old Frenchie X Dachshund who loves people and enjoys fuss, greeting you with her trademark bouncy wiggle. Pooky is looking to be the only dog in the home, and would prefer to go for walks in less dog populated areas but has great focus on her handler. She is looking to live with secondary school aged children who are confident with her excitable play style. 
The Dachshund side of her means she can be vocal when she's left alone for too long, so a family who is able to build up those leaving hours slowly at first would be ideal for her. Pooky needs her own private garden where she can chill and enjoy her alone time during the day before cuddling up on the sofa in the evening. She loves her food, and is very receptive to training so will be such a fun dog to spend time with. Pooky has a few tricks up her sleeve such as spin, down and paw and would love for her brain to be kept busy in her new home. Pooky is smashing her muzzle training, and is comfortable wearing this for her walks. She will make a wonderful addition to the home!

Pooky is sure to bring a joyful, fun-loving energy to your home. She does enjoy a play with her toys, but much prefers rough housing and playing chase with her favourite people. She is a very clever girl who has several tricks in her wheelhouse that she loves to do with her humans for a tasty treat or two (ham is her favourite). Pooky walks well on lead and prefers a quiet, sniffy walk where she won't be bothered by any other dogs, as she finds them quite worrying. Since being in our care she has made great progress around other dogs and is doing really well at passing them at a respectable distance with little to no reaction. Because of this, she will need owners who want to keep up with her training and who are able to advocate for her and give her space from other dogs when out in public. After a long day of playing and sniffing, she loves nothing more than a fuss and a cuddle with her favourite people. This sweet girl is full of personality and we can't wait for her to find her forever home.

name: Miranda
description:
Miranda is looking for a loving, patient home where she can continue to build her confidence at her own pace. She will need a home with no other pets and can live with primary school-aged children, provided they are calm and respectful around her. Miranda can be left for 1-4 hours once she has settled in, with this built up gradually and sensitively. A quieter home environment would suit her best, where she can enjoy a predictable routine and plenty of reassurance as she adjusts to her new surroundings.

Miranda is a gentle five-year-old Corgi who is really showing her sweet personality now she has settled into foster care! She's a total people lover who enjoys a fuss, will happily lean in for a cuddle and has a particular soft spot for children. At home, she's generally calm and relaxed, enjoying her toys, treats and a good snooze on the sofa. She also enjoys getting out for walks, where she loves to sniff and explore, although busy traffic and unfamiliar surroundings can make her a little unsure. Having had a challenging start in life, Miranda is still learning about the world and will need kind, patient adopters who are happy introduce her to lots of positive experiences.

name: Polly Pocket
description:
Sweet and sensitive ball of fluff Polly Pocket is a 2 and a half year old Pomeranian cross who is full of affection once she gets to know you. She is quite the adventurer and loves a good sniff and explore on her walks. Initially Polly can be quite independent, but once she has built a bond she will become your little shadow, following you around and nudging your arm for fusses, she may even climb into your lap for ultimate snuggle time. Give her space and she will reward you for it. This super fluffer is ready to find her new family.

Polly Pocket is looking for a calm and predictable home with loving and adopters who can take her on sniffy strolls, who will take the time to help her settle in and give her all the love and care she deserves. She is a sweet girl but does need time to get to know new people so could live with secondary school children who will let her approach at her pace, play with her nicely and give her space to rest and relax when needed. Polly is friendly girl but does prefer all of the attention and toys to herself so would like to be the only pet in the home, she would be happy with calm and confident walking friends. Polly can be encouraged to engage in training if a tasty treat is on offer. Polly would like her own private, secure garden where she can enjoy exploring at her leisure. Polly can be a little worried being left, so is look for someone home the majority of the time especially to begin with, any leaving time would need to be built up slowly once she has had time to settle into her new home. Polly will need to meet her adopters a few times prior to going home, so please bear all of this in mind when applying.

name: Molly
description:
